entries.line: **Breaking: `abcd ideate record` takes only a version-2 verdict.** A version-1 payload is refused with a message naming version 2, and so is a verdict with a record id that does not resolve in any leg, a primary source that is not an https address, a filed source key or a record id, a grill with no hits and no recorded searches, or a claim marked verified whose only primary source is the idea's own. The grill records each search as its terms, places and count, and a claim checked only against the idea's own source reads quoted. Anything that writes verdicts moves to the version-2 shape the `ideate` command page shows; verdicts already on record are left as they are.

**Breaking: a reframed or split ideate verdict must say so.** A reframed verdict must carry its reframing and any other verdict must not; the record renders it under The reframing. Each reviewer is recorded under its own label with its own kill attempts, verdict and consulted sources, one idea per reviewer context, and a split between reviewers is refused unless the ruling that settled it names who ruled, the verdict and the reason.

**Breaking: the sites abcd builds publish no person's name.** The contributors page and `record.json` give human authors only as a count of people and of their commits: no author name, login or profile link reaches a page or the JSON, and the health page's same-author panel is withdrawn. A project site shows no git-history details (authors, declared models, commit counts or dates) and its build reads no git history. Anything that read author names or profile links from `record.json` must stop relying on them.

**A session left to work on keeps working while it has work.** `abcd mode autonomous` (optionally `--until <time>`) records once for the repository, with who set it and when it ends, that sessions work on while the person is away, and repeats it at every session start, compaction and prompt. A session that tries to end its turn with work it can still do alone is handed the next item, a question it would have asked is decided and recorded, and an act only the person may approve is queued with `abcd mode queue`; `abcd mode back` ends the mode and lists what was queued and any stop the host forced. When a git read passes its deadline, the owed-work reading is marked incomplete and the session is let stop. The mode grants nothing: what a session may push stays whatever the person's own instructions say.

**A repository says who merges, and abcd keeps to it.** `facilitator.mode` in `.abcd/config.json` is `human` (the default) or `auto`. With `human`, a maintainer's ready pull request waits for the technical facilitator's approval and abcd arms the merge only once it is given, whoever asks; with `auto`, a maintainer's pull request that has passed its gates and its review pair goes into the merge queue, or has auto-merge armed where the forge has no queue, and the status line says merging is autonomous. A contributor's pull request waits for a maintainer's approval in either mode, and `human` set on the person's own machine always wins, so installing abcd changes nothing about who merges.

**Private security reports stay private until their fix ships.** `abcd embargo` brings each private security advisory from GitHub into a private record on the person's own machine that never enters the public ledger, records the verdict and who gave it, closes on GitHub, with the explanation the person approved, an advisory judged not abcd's or not a vulnerability, and checks every commit message, pull-request body and record about to go public for anything that would give an advisory away. Once the release carrying the fixes is cut it shows the publication plan with each patched version; on one explicit yes it publishes one advisory, checks it went out as planned, then publishes the rest. Advisories have their own commands; the drain's rule is unchanged.

**abcd audits and applies a repository's GitHub settings.** `abcd ahoy --remote` reports, read-only, how a managed repository's GitHub settings differ from a safe baseline, one line per setting with what it is now and what it should be; `abcd ahoy remote apply` turns on what is missing on a yes and writes down what it changed. It never changes whether a repository is public or private and never requires a check the repository's own workflows do not run. Each required check is pinned to the one app observed reporting it, and a check whose source is unclear stays on any source and is named. A setting the plan does not offer is listed as owed, and a repository can ask for a setting to be left alone in its own reviewed config.

**A run records what it was actually run with.** Every model call, through the host, a command-line runner or a provider connection, records what abcd asked for (model, settings sent, prompt hash, harness version) and what answered (served model, provider, generation id, finish reason, token counts, cost); a field the route cannot show is named with its reason, never guessed. `abcd ahoy connect` verifies a new connection with a usage-in-stream request and, when the server refuses it with HTTP 400 or 422, asks again without it, writes `stream_usage: false` into the block it creates and says so; `--stream-usage` sets the value outright.

**After a plugin update, abcd says what changed and offers the setup that waits.** The next session's first reply gives one line per release, from a short digest each release carries inside abcd; `abcd update news` prints those lines, and `abcd update news --full` gives the full summary: what waits on this repository and anything that now needs the person to act. When the update brings setup the repository needs, the reply offers to run setup again, which then asks only the new questions. Noticing the update reads only what is on disk, never the internet, and nothing changes without a yes.

**Every contributor commits as themselves.** Each person's commit identity is kept on their own machine, in the abcd home (`identity.json`, or `identity/<root-sha>.json` for one repository); the commit check, `abcd ahoy --identity` and the committed pre-commit gate hold commits to that record and never read a committed pin, so no contributor is told to commit under the maintainer's name. A commit made under a bot's or an AI tool's name is still refused, a mistyped email of one's own is still caught, and setup moves a committed `.abcd/config/identity.json` to its owner's machine.

**Setup installs the tools abcd needs for the person alone, checked.** A tool such as a secret scanner is installed with no admin rights into the person's own bin folder, as a download pinned in abcd's release and checked by sha256 (and, for gh, its signed build record) before anything runs; a copy the person already has is used, and setup says plainly how far each download could be checked. Homebrew is not the install step and no sudo advice is ever relayed. `abcd update` and the tool installer share one download rule, and each purpose reaches only its own hosts.

**Setup offers to put abcd's folder on the PATH.** When the folder abcd installs into is not on the person's PATH, setup asks once whether to add it to their shell settings, changes them only on a yes, never adds the same line twice, and undoes the change when abcd is removed; declined, the line to add is on the checklist at the end of setup.

**An opted-in project's record is built onto its own GitHub Pages.** When a public project switches it on at setup, its own release workflow builds the project's about page and development record at each release and publishes them on the project's GitHub Pages. Every page opens with a line saying it is the record of an abcd-managed repository, linking to the repository, and every word on it comes from the repository; GitHub hosts it and abcd runs nothing.

**The hooks can run the latest reviewed branch of a checkout.** A checkout listed in `dogfood-roots` in the abcd home (the checkout, a tab, the URL of a remote no agent can move, and optionally a tab and a branch, `main` when left out) runs, in every hook and through the command pages, a build of that branch's tip as the declared remote reports it; nothing in the checkout chooses it. Until that build is ready, or when it dies, the installed release runs. A remote on localhost or a loopback address is refused, a bracketed scp-like host is refused with its own reason, the store keeps every build a recorded tip names, and the docs name git's own inherited environment among what the build still takes from the account.

The brief session page asks for no relay address or token: it finds its relay from the repository's `relays.json` or the invite link, or is served by the host's own computer, signs in with GitHub, and opens on the brief's press release in plain words.

**abcd's closed-option judgements can run through a decision adapter.** The adapter answers with a value and a calibrated probability; it runs in shadow as a lab first, recorded beside the host's answer, and a research note turns a judgement over to it. Embark's lesson ranking is such a judgement: `abcd embark lessons` asks one score question per lesson and ranks by the scores, with term overlap breaking ties.

**The shell guard answers the permission prompts of agents abcd starts.** A headless claude launch whose role may use the shell carries `abcd guard approve` as the harness's permission prompt tool: a command the guard reads whole and clears runs, and anything else is refused with the guard's reason. While a build or drain runs for the checkout or one of its lanes, abcd refuses the host's approval prompt for a shell command it cannot check, telling the agent to rewrite it into plain checkable steps or skip it; it never grants one, and build and drain say so as they start.

**The shell guard refuses deleting a branch or removing a worktree it cannot prove spent.** A local or remote branch delete and a `git worktree remove` run only when the target is merged into origin's default branch, has no open pull request, is in no worktree and is held by no reservation, and a worktree must also be clean and in use by nothing; a check that cannot answer refuses. The person alone can allow one exact line once with `abcd guard allow`.

**The shell guard checks pull-request text before it posts.** Where a repository sets `outbound.forge: true` in `.abcd/config.json`, a `gh pr create`, `new` or `edit` whose body carries no `Assisted-by` line in an accepted form is blocked (`forge-text-disclosure`), and, where `outbound.declare_mentions` is also set, so is one whose title and body name an issue id that no `Resolves:` or `Refs:` line declares (`forge-text-mention`). The bundled COMMITTING rule names pull-request bodies beside commits.

**`abcd land` composes the pull-request body.** With no pull request open, it composes the body from the branch's commits (subjects and their `Refs:`, `Resolves:`, `Delivers:` and `Assisted-by:` lines), judges it with the shell guard's body checks, writes it to the local tier in a file named after the branch and its head commit, and prints the `gh pr create` that uses it; a body file already there is kept, judged and said so, so an edit survives a second run. `abcd land` and a build or drain lane's landing post `merging <item>` and push only once it is on origin, so a colleague's status read shows it before the branch exists there; a hand-typed `git push` posts none.

**A release reservation holds every merge, including those armed before it.** `abcd reserve rel-vX.Y.Z` withdraws each auto-merge and merge-queue entry already armed, records each withdrawal on its branch, admits a merge only by `--admit`, refuses the cut while an unadmitted merge is armed, and re-arms exactly what it withdrew when the release ends; each act is commented on the pull request. The hold's hand remedy for a queued pull request points at taking it out of the merge queue or at `--admit`, and every hand remedy says that nothing re-arms what it disarms.

**Spent reservation branches are deleted from the forge.** `abcd reserve --sweep` judges each reservation branch and, under the reservation-sweep workflow's App token, deletes the spent ones; a branch whose tip is a plain release is spent at the next sweep once the take-over margin has passed, and any other tip still waits its age. The reservations ruleset names that App as its only bypass.

**`abcd peers` says which copy holds each reservation.** Each reservation names this copy, the other worktree of the repository on this machine that made it (by its folder name), or elsewhere. The reader's live reservations are counted by copy against `reservation.max_live`, with a warning from four fifths of it that every session and account on the same login counts toward one total; the cap refusal groups the held records by copy, and the own-copy overlap warning of `abcd reserve` names the other copy.

`abcd reserve` and `abcd build` warn when a footprint names a directory, giving its tracked file count, and a build reserves exactly the files its spec names. `abcd reserve` names each generated file a footprint shares with another live reservation, and that reservation's record, and a renewal or take-over of one's own hold names each held path the new footprint drops (`dropped_footprint`).

**A main checkout that two or more live sessions started in refuses writes.** The record writers (`capture`, `intent`, `decide`, `spec close` and the index generator) refuse there with exit 3 and name the worktree store, and the guard hook denies the host's own file tools a write there outside the local tier; the session hooks keep one occupancy marker per session.

**A load-gate waiter says who holds the gate and how busy it is.** Every waiting line names each holder ahead with its age and its process tree's CPU over the last ten minutes, said again every ten minutes while the gate stays shut; a holder whose tree has used no more than a tenth of a core for ten minutes is reported as quiet, on the waiters' lines and on its own stderr. It is a report, not a diagnosis: nothing is signalled, and a tree of short-lived children can still read as working.

`abcd drain --skip <iss-N|path> --reason <why>` holds back an issue, or every issue whose `found_at` lies in a path, for the drain in progress; each move passes it over with the reason, `--unskip` lifts it, and the list clears when the drain ends.

`abcd implement step --route <role>=runner:<name>[@<provider>/<model>]` runs one step's role on a named runner and allowlisted model, refusing an unknown or disabled runner and an unlisted model before anything is written, and records the route in the role's receipt.

A machine provider block on an OpenRouter base URL can pin a model to exactly one upstream provider and one quantisation (`oracle.api.<provider>.pins`, with fallbacks off and data collection denied); each call sends the provider routing object and records it as the provider pin, and with `read_generation: true` the generation is read back after each call to record what served it.

A machine provider block takes a local pin per model (runtime, version, weights digest, quantisation, context length, KV-cache type, and on llama.cpp the GGUF file's name); the server is probed before a pinned route runs, a mismatch is refused naming the fix, and the record carries the pin and what the server reported. A runner route whose provider is a block on this machine records `local: true` and lists the local fields, as not configured when there is no pin.

`abcd intent ready` and record-lint (`spec_steps_serial`, a warning) flag a multi-step spec with no `needs` line, and planning asks for each step's needs, so steps that do not depend on each other are not held one behind another.
Two waiters in one copy renew its reservations in turn under a per-copy lock, so the second finds nothing due rather than reporting the first's renewals as failures.

The preflight's govulncheck scan, on a branch that changes no dependency, also scans the fork point and only warns when the fork point reports every finding the branch does; a finding only the branch reports, or a fork point that cannot be scanned, stops the preflight.
A command abcd stops when its context ends is reported as stopped by that context, even when its pipes close before the wait sees the end.

The setup command page and the brief's identity, site, embargo and ideate chapters state what abcd does now: the settings mirror is read by a reviewer, the identity move says what keeps a record and what blocks it, uninstall reports the shell-settings line it removes, the update, ideate and embargo pages say what abcd does, and the embargo triage example names a role.

**A preflight waits for its turn as one whole run.** `make preflight` takes the load gate once for the whole run: a queued run does no lint, eval, build, vet or test work until the gate admits it, so the runs waiting never add to the load the running one is judged by. Whole runs are admitted as many at once as `load.preflights` allows (one by default), the setting is read again at every look so a change reaches runs already queued, the wait's report names the value it judged by and where it came from, and a records-only change takes a shorter preflight that waits at no gate.

**Reservation and announcement commits name no login.** Their trailers and the status branch name carry an opaque holder id, minted once per machine account and kept in the abcd home, and holds made before are still read as the person's own. A copy on an older release reads the new holds as held until it updates, and a person running two versions renews only from the new one; a hosted or ephemeral session keeps one id by setting `ABCD_HOLDER_ID`.

**Closing a session keeps its transcript.** The SessionEnd hook runs no git: it stages the raw transcript by session id into a machine-level pending folder, and the next session start (or a history drain) files, redacts and stores it, so the host does not cancel the hook on a loaded machine. A transcript that cannot be placed is named and kept, `abcd history discard --pending` removes one by hand, and a person on an older plugin gets this with the plugin update.

**A lapsed hold is lifted without a person.** Every release-hold line names when the hold lapses, and once it has, nothing holds the merge; `abcd status` and `abcd peers` name an expired release reservation with no tag on origin as a lapsed cut holding no merge, with how a cut resumes, and the prompt hook names each lapsed cut once, so a crashed holder's cut is not relayed as live.

A reservation stays live while its holder waits: `abcd implement load --wait` renews the caller's own live reservations from this copy once each is half through its lease, while it waits and while its command runs, `abcd implement status` renews the runs it shows, and a build's lapsed reservation revived later is judged against the person's other copy only on the files the run's lanes changed.

Each test stage of `make preflight` gives every package a 40-minute budget, doubled when the one-minute load passes one runnable per core as the stage starts, so a loaded machine's unit stage is not killed at twenty minutes with no test hung.

A preflight queued at its race gate takes no first-gate slot until its race run starts, so another preflight's unit stage can run meanwhile; `load.preflights` takes 1 to 4 and is described everywhere as how many whole preflight runs the first gate admits at once, with one race stage able to run beside them.

The load gate's queue stays first-come-first-served after macOS process ids wrap: every waiter that started earlier counts as ahead whatever its pid, and a wait stops counting waiters from an older abcd that cross it once they alone have held its gate shut for five minutes.

The load gate refuses, without waiting, a preflight's test or race stage, and any command run through `abcd implement load --wait`, while the volume holding the Go build cache or the worktree store has less free space than its floor (4 GiB per preflight admitted at once, 8 GiB at least), naming each low volume and offering a trim of build-cache entries unused for two days.
The load gate's waiting line names, by pid, the `go test` runs outside the gate that keep the load up, and the LOAD rules domain teaches gating a package's tests.

The ruthless, docs-currency and security reviewer definitions run no tests, builds or project code and ask the author for gated test evidence, so a review on a shared machine adds no ungated test run.

A git command run under a deadline ends at that deadline: the partial-clone guard's version probe and config read take the caller's deadline (30 seconds where there is none), and a deadline-bound read takes git's whole output before waiting on git, so an answer git gave is not lost on a loaded machine.

A burst of sub-agent stops on a loaded machine stages every transcript: a failed git lookup is retried within the hook's budget rather than read as no repository, and a transcript still not staged is counted in a marker that `abcd history staged` reports.
A session started with `--name` makes the session-start hook ask git nothing for it.

`abcd reserve`, the release hold and `abcd peers` name a sibling worktree on this machine as that worktree rather than as another computer, from one reading of the worktrees: siblings whose folders share names read by the fewest trailing folders that tell them apart, the ceiling counts siblings by copy key, and the cap refusal names copies from each holder's own live tips and says why the worktrees could not be listed.
Reading the reservations (`abcd peers`, the status line, the sweep's dry run) writes nothing into the git object store.
`abcd reserve` drops a footprint path named twice, so a renewal that repeats the held footprint stays under the message size cap.

A build reserves each entry of a spec's Footprint packages line by its leading path, dropping a trailing note and not splitting on a comma inside it; an entry that is still prose refuses the start, naming the spec and the entry.
abcd reads the generated-file declarations in `.gitattributes` as git does: a blank or comment line decides nothing whatever bytes it holds, so a non-ASCII comment does not void every declaration.

`abcd build` counts a peer as holding an intent only when it holds the record in another folder and changed it since their merge-base, so an old local branch carrying the default branch's unchanged copy does not block a build.
The implement loop's landing marks a lane's spec step landed in its records commit, so `spec close --remainder` and a fresh `abcd build` do not carry or reopen steps that already merged.
Two implement runs started in the same second list in start order, so a handed-back run is not read as the newer one and a record read is not refused as two runs in progress.
A drain state written by a newer abcd is refused as a newer abcd's, telling the person to run that abcd and keep the file, rather than as a file that does not parse.

The pre-push hook passes an empty-tree reservation or announcement pushed from a shallow clone, such as a hosted session's, and still refuses a push that changes a file, a rewrite, or a range reaching past the shallow line.

Hosted cloud setup gives the normal user it creates a read-only, root-owned copy of each proxy CA bundle that user cannot read, so networked git works as that user; TLS verification is never turned off.
The cloud hand-back's closing line says the report could not go with the work, which holds for every fallback to the tracking issue, rather than saying a push failed.
The cloud launch connector refuses an environment id that is not self-hosted before it asks the host, saying why; only a self-hosted environment can be started this way.

`abcd embargo publish` plans an advisory from the fix commit its private record names when the release carries no public record of it, and prints the command that restores the record after publication.

Embargo intake and every publication plan read each held advisory's state on GitHub, so an advisory published outside `abcd embargo publish` is recorded as published and released from `abcd embargo check`; a close is recorded only under a verdict that ends the private track.

`abcd embargo check --range` reads a merge commit for the lines it adds against every parent, so text a merge of the default branch brings in is not judged as the branch's own, and an advisory id no store holds passes when GitHub lists it among the repository's published advisories.

A verdict abcd leaves to the person, such as embargo triage, is asked with each item's evidence, the verdict the evidence supports and why the others do not fit, and is recorded only on the person's yes.

A status move such as `abcd capture resolve` writes the record at its new path with the mode it had, so a record kept 0600 in the embargo store stays 0600 and the embargo verbs keep reading the store.

Setup saves each config value on its own: a value deferred with decide later, or answered with something setup does not write, stays unset and is listed as remaining, while every answered value and every value passed by flag is written, in a full `abcd ahoy install` and with `--only-waiting`; a refused deep-scan answer draws a note naming the accepted answers and `--scan-deep`.

**A clone whose committed git hooks do not run is named.** Session start says so, on stderr and to the session, and setup asks at a terminal, as its own question, to set `core.hooksPath` to `.githooks`, listing the command when it cannot ask; setup does not report clean while the committed hooks do not run.
Setup asks about the commit identity as its own question at a terminal, never listed under or declined by the settings approval.
Setup run from a plain terminal offers the abcd download before the status line, and does not ask about the status line when it cannot be wired.
abcd reports the install mode from the copy the recorded PATH entry names when no plugin root resolves, so a working README install does not read as nothing installed.
In a source checkout of abcd, a `go run` build of the checkout being installed is treated as current, so `abcd ahoy install` does not refuse it as a stale binary.

The staleness line of bare `abcd ahoy` and `abcd --version` names what it compared against: the checkout tip for a source build, or the plugin manifest pin for a pinned install, with `abcd update --check` named as the way to compare with the newest release.
`abcd ahoy remote apply` names the settings it already changed on GitHub when it refuses after one, instead of saying nothing was changed.
`abcd ahoy install` leaves out of its `.gitignore` block any entry the file already lists in force, so no entry is written twice.

`abcd site setup` creates the site-render and site environments admitting only the default branch, reports an existing tag rule as one to remove, and the workflow it writes runs a published release from the default branch.
A step whose chat call to the person's own model server never got an answer falls back to the agent harness, saying whether a size count or model listing had already reached the server.
The opencode runner leaves the served model empty and listed as not reported, since its run mode names none, rather than recording the model it asked for as the model that answered.
The shell guard reads a syntax check such as `bash -n <file>` as running nothing, so a script that a run would refuse can still be checked; startup files are still judged.
The shell guard's forge-text check reads a short-flag cluster as gh does, so a body given behind boolean shorthands, as in `gh pr create -db '<text>'`, is judged.

`abcd capture`, and the consistency ingest for every finding it files, hold a record's body to the site renderer's check before writing, so a body the renderer refuses is refused at the write rather than at the next gate run.

A consistency report too large for the reviews board keeps its header and findings table in `00-summary.md` and writes each finding in full to `01-findings.md`; a pass whose table alone is too large is refused before any finding is filed.

The reflect seed treats an owed review marker as not audited and lists the intents the cut moved to next; an Audit Notes section with no marker counts as audited only when it names the acceptance criteria and gives a verdict on them.
abcd reads a checkout's local-tier state only when git tracks none of it, and record-lint refuses a change that tracks a file there.
`abcd ideate record` writes the private store when no visibility flag is given, `--public` stays the opt-in, and `/abcd:ideate` states that default instead of asking before every run.
The comments on capture's promotion request say its grounds are optional, as the code reads them.

abcd's repository names no organisation member in its tracked files: it carries no code-owners file, mailmap or committed identity pin, the citation names the organisation, and the scanner and test fixtures use personas.

abcd builds on Go 1.26.10, which carries the standard library's fix for GO-2026-6809 (crypto/x509: distrust compromised intermediate certificates), and every CI setup step and the preflight read that version from `go.mod`.

A release's notes do not describe a fix to a surface no earlier release had as a Fixed line: the cut marks a record whose path the previous tag did not hold and lists the commands that tag lacked, and the changelog ingest refuses a Fixed line citing such a record.

**Sessions name themselves.** Each session takes a persona name at its first prompt (Alice, Bob, Carol and on through the repository's persona list), shown in its status line, its prompt border and the session list other sessions message it from. A name the person gave keeps, a resumed or compacted session keeps its name, and no two live sessions under one account on the machine share a name, even in different repositories. Naming works on macOS and Linux; where it cannot, a session starts unnamed and is never blocked.

**A drain runs unattended.** The drain's judgement of each remedy is a drain-judge role on the runner routing, answered and taken in one move with abcd computing the remedy digest, so no person writes the answer by hand; `abcd drain --take-over` moves a person's own reservations from a lost copy, such as a restarted hosted session, as the drain reaches them.
`abcd peers` lists each live reservation's drain stage and each holder's hand-backs of the last day with their kinds, so a person can see what another account's drain is doing.

A running drain takes a new `--pace`, `--sub-agents` and `--fix-rounds`, applied from the next lane and from the next stage of the lane in progress; a handed-back issue whose record changed on origin is judged afresh, and an old handed-back run no longer passes its issue over.

`reservation.max_live` in the person's own `~/.abcd.noindex/config.json` sets the per-person reservation cap, from 1 to 100 and ten when unset; it is read from the machine layer alone, and the cap refusal names the setting.

A release cut is held by a reservation of the release, `rel-vX.Y.Z`: every other session's landing step, the implement loop's land fence and `abcd land`, reads it and refuses to merge while it is live, and `abcd peers` shows the hold.

A bundled `SCRATCH` rules domain tells an agent that the host's scratchpad holds only a turn's throwaway files, because it does not survive a reboot or a new session, so anything a later turn, session or agent reads goes in the main checkout's local tier or under `~/.abcd.noindex/`; and that before writing a helper script it checks whether an abcd command already does the job.

**Drains on several accounts share the work.** Each drain move fetches origin and plans from what origin's default branch holds, never from a checkout that has fallen behind; the dry run names its view's age, the commits behind and the issues finished there, and a reservation of an issue already finished there backs off.

A drain reserves an issue before it asks for the judgement over it, passes over an issue or footprint another copy holds with no judgement and no fetch, and takes each group of the queue in its own order, file-scoped issues first, so several drains no longer all judge the head of the queue.

A drain's hand-back is recorded on origin, so every account's drain passes over the issue until a person changes its record; an issue whose related intents name an intent is handed back as promoted and is not judged or promoted again.

At the per-person reservation cap a drain move waits for a pull request to merge instead of refusing, keeps the judgements it was given and names the pull requests waiting; the cap's refusal advises waiting for a merge rather than releasing a reservation.

Every drain move renews the lane in progress at half its lease, so a lane the host pauses keeps its reservation, and the landing checks the reservation before its push, so a lapsed lease taken over by another account pushes nothing and opens no duplicate pull request.

A fresh reservation refuses when origin is a fork, naming its parent and the command that repoints origin, rather than reserving where no other account looks; renewals and releases never ask, and a forge that does not answer warns and lets the reservation through.
A sibling worktree or branch the drain cannot read stops the move once, naming it and the repair, instead of making every issue read as held by someone else.

A drain whose remaining eligible issues are all held by others waits, says when it looks again, names the holds and keeps its judgements; it stops as empty only when nothing eligible is left, held or not.

A drain lane's reservation narrows at its landing to the files its branch changed within its footprint, so an issue scoped to a whole directory no longer locks other accounts out of every file under it; the lane re-reserves its whole footprint before a fresh round.

**A stuck drain lane hands itself back.** A lane that keeps refusing is handed back as stuck after three identical refusals or sixty minutes at one stage, or at once when the refusal cannot change; its reservation is released and the drain takes up the next issue. A wait by design is never counted as a refusal, and `abcd implement step --discard` ends a stuck lane's run.

Each drain move reads every lane parked at landing from one listing of the person's pull requests: a closed one is handed back and its reservation released, a conflicting one is no longer renewed and is named, and an open one is renewed and named as waiting.

An issue lane merges origin's default branch before its push whenever it has moved; a conflict on files declared as generated goes back to the implementer to regenerate, any other conflict hands the lane back naming the files with nothing pushed, and a waiting pull request that starts to conflict on generated files alone syncs again.
Every lane a drain opens starts on the drain's own pace and sub-agent ceiling, not only the first.
A drain move that cannot fetch origin or read its default branch waits on the outage schedule instead of refusing.
Reservation acts ask the forge who the person is once per process rather than on every act, and ask again after an account switch, a login or a logout.
The pre-push hook reads every pushed commit exactly as it is stored, so the reservation and status checks judge the same files the push sends.
The embargo store is found from the root commit of origin's default branch, so a checkout whose current branch has a different history no longer misses the store and reads nothing as under embargo.

A hosted cloud session sets its clone's author identity from the environment's forge token before any commit, so its commits carry the person's identity rather than the host's default one; it says once when it cannot, without showing the identity the container came with.
The cloud launch connector recognises a refused start even when the host's answer spreads its error over more than one line, so a refused start is no longer reported as started.

A cloud hand-back run twice with an unchanged report no longer reports a refused commit: a report that is already the branch's last commit is pushed as it stands, and one an earlier commit holds falls back saying so.
The load gate queues waiters by when they started rather than by process id alone, so a waiter is no longer starved once the machine's process ids wrap.

`abcd land` asks origin for its default branch when the checkout's own record of it is stale or missing, instead of refusing and handing the person a manual step; a forge and origin that disagree, or an origin that cannot be asked, still refuse, and the default-branch refusal no longer carries an unrelated hint.

`abcd peers` judges each release hold by the same rule as the landing steps, so in a checkout without its local tier it no longer lists as holding merges a release hold that `abcd land` does not count; `--json` release holds carry `own` and `unsighted`.
A status fetch reads an app's push to a status branch as an app's, so the branch is no longer asked about again on every fetch with a line saying the record does not yet name its tip.

The shell guard refuses a `bash -c` or `sh -c` script built from variables that deletes files, and its refusal and the `SHELL` rules give the rewrite, so an agent writes a command the host can check instead of stalling at the host's permission prompt.
The asking rules tell an agent to redraft a refused or over-limit question silently, so the person sees only the finished question.
The launch hook-compliance gate judges a hook file's mode only where the hook text executes it, so a script run through `sh` or `bash` is no longer reported as not executable.
The `abcd ideate` refusal of a malformed grill citation lists `dcn-N` among the citable forms, as the citation grammar accepts it.
The inbox's promotion rewrite writes a sender's `dcn-N` id as one word, as it already did for the other record families, so it never cites abcd's own decision record.
`abcd update --help` says build provenance is pinned to abcd's release workflow on main, as the verb requires.
The update command page's by-hand provenance check carries `--deny-self-hosted-runners`, matching the check abcd itself applies.
The reservation status tests allow a fixed tenfold slack on their timing bounds and log the measured time, so they no longer fail on a heavily loaded machine.

The press release of the reservations intent no longer quotes a persona saying a person's copies never lock each other out; it now says what shipped, that moving a piece of work from one of a person's copies to another is one flag.

The design brief's update chapter describes the verb as it shipped: it names every network reach (the launch preview and release cut when they read a published baseline, and GitHub's API and Sigstore's TUF repository for the provenance check that update and an ahoy installation both make), the build-provenance verification beside the checksums, the `attested_by` receipt field, the newest-release mark with its `older-than-mark` refusal, and all three refusals that arrive after dispatch.

The design brief's configuration chapter names every key the binary reads, `reservation.github_username`, the consistency keys and `readme.parts` among them, lists the README question among those install asks, and says the bootstrap hook holds its download to the build-provenance policy as well as the checksums.

**Reservations on the shared remote.** When an agent starts on an item, abcd reserves it for the person the agent works for, as a branch on `origin` (`abcd-reserved/<record-id>`) that nobody merges, so everyone who works on the project sees it from any computer or cloud session. `abcd build` reserves the intent it starts, `abcd drain` reserves each issue it takes, and `abcd reserve <record-id> --footprint <path>…` (with `--release` to give it back) covers work started by hand. Every reservation names the paths the work expects to change; one held by someone else, or one whose paths overlap a live reservation, is refused naming who holds it and until when. A reservation lasts two hours, is renewed while the work goes on, and stops counting once its record is terminal on the default branch. `abcd peers` lists every reservation with its holder, footprint, expiry and state, and `build next` passes over an item another person holds.

**Every decision is its own record.** A decision is now one minted `dcn-` file in the flat folder `.abcd/work/decisions/`, so two branches that each record a decision merge with no conflict and no merge attribute. `abcd decide` with no operand and the site's Decision log list every decision, newest first. Breaking: abcd's own `.abcd/work/DECISIONS.md` is gone, with its entries converted to their own files and every link to it rewritten, and the decisions-append gate is retired, so anything that read or linked the single file must follow the decision's own file instead. A repository abcd manages keeps its existing `DECISIONS.md` untouched as frozen history and records new decisions in the folder.

**`abcd decide "<text>"` records a decision; `abcd decide --adr "<title>"` mints an ADR.** Breaking: the bare form no longer mints an ADR, so a script or habit that ran `abcd decide "<title>"` for an ADR must add `--adr`. An earlier release's binary still mints an ADR for the bare form.

**One outbound opt-in.** `ahoy install --outbound` turns on both the commit-message check and the shell guard's forge-text check at once. Breaking: `--outbound-hook` and `--outbound-forge` are removed and refused at exit 2 with a message naming `--outbound`, writing nothing; pass `--outbound` instead. A repository that recorded only one half under the old flags is reported, and the next `ahoy install` completes it under the settings approval.

**`abcd land [<branch>]` lands any branch, not only a build lane.** It skips the gate when a preflight receipt names HEAD, otherwise runs `make preflight` in the branch's checkout and requires HEAD unchanged and a receipt, then plain-pushes the branch to `origin` with hooks on, never forced and never the default branch. `land.push` (default on) turns the push off from any config layer, and `--no-push` for one run; when off, it prints the push command and names the layer.

**`abcd land` queues a ready pull request straight away.** After pushing, it arms the branch's open pull request and confirms it is in the merge queue, never waiting on earlier entries and never changing the repository's or the queue's settings, so the queue can build as many entries at once as it is configured to. `land.enqueue` (default on) and `--no-enqueue` switch it off. It opens no pull request: with none, it prints the command that opens one. Where no merge queue gates the default branch with a required approval, it says the merge is left to a person.

`ahoy install --outbound` now sets this clone's `git config --local abcd.binary` itself, to the absolute path of the abcd copy on PATH that the same run verified, so the commit-message check runs without a hand step; it writes nothing, and says why, for a copy that did not verify, the dev shim, a relative path or a copy inside the working tree, and leaves a value the person already set. Where no hooks path is set and no `commit-msg` hook exists, it also installs abcd's commit-message hook in the shared git directory; it never replaces an existing hook, never sets `core.hooksPath` and never touches global config, and otherwise saves the hook under a name git never runs and says how to call it.

`abcd land` no longer has to be run twice after a push that moves the branch: it re-reads the pull request's head every 2 seconds for up to 30 seconds and arms once the forge shows the pushed commit, and on timeout it still stops and says how long it waited.

A pull request the land step leaves waiting on a person now keeps its reservation on the shared remote for a day whether or not the checkout has a ruleset mirror, instead of losing it after two hours without one, when a colleague's drain could take the record and redo the work.

**The shell guard can check text before it reaches the forge.** `abcd ahoy install --outbound-forge` opts a repository in: the title, body and body file (`--title`/`-t`, `--body`/`-b`, `--body-file`/`-F`) of a `gh pr` or `gh issue` create, new, edit or comment command are checked before the command runs. This adds two reserved guard ids. A live agent-session URL or a tool attribution footer blocks the command under `forge-text-outbound`, without echoing the text. Text the guard could not check warns under `forge-text-unread`: a body file it cannot read or place, a body file written earlier on the same line, a broken `pii.json`, or a line carrying more than sixteen texts. The check is never on by default, is recorded as `outbound.forge: true` in `.abcd/config.json`, and is separate from `--outbound-hook`. It does not cover `--body-file -`, `--editor`, `--web`, `--fill`, `--template`, posting from inside a script the line runs, `gh api`, `gh pr review`, `gh release`, `gh pr merge --body`, or any forge client other than `gh`. For those, re-read what was posted.

**An opt-in commit-message gate for managed repositories.** `abcd ahoy install --outbound-hook` adds a committed commit-msg hook. It runs `abcd lint outbound` and refuses a commit message carrying a live agent-session URL or a tool attribution footer. The hook is never installed by default. It runs only the abcd named by an absolute path in `git config --local abcd.binary`, never one found on PATH or in the working tree, and it lets the commit through with one warning when none is usable. Set `abcd.binary` and `core.hooksPath` by hand in each clone, because `ahoy install` writes neither. The hook checks commit messages only; forge text is the `--outbound-forge` check.

**abcd's home keeps itself out of a dotfiles repository.** The first abcd command that runs with `~/.abcd.noindex` in place writes `~/.abcd.noindex/.gitignore` holding `*`, readable by your account alone. After that, a `git add -A` in a home folder kept in git stages nothing abcd keeps there. abcd writes the file once: if you delete it, abcd leaves it deleted, and that is how you let your home repository track abcd's home. The status line never writes it. In a read-only home, the command still runs and prints one line on stderr saying the file was not written (no line under `--json` or in a hook call). The file does not untrack anything your home repository already tracks, and credentials are still refused inside any git working tree whatever the file says.

**`abcd ideate record` asks whether a verdict is private or public.** It takes exactly one of `--private` or `--public` and refuses without one, so a call without either now stops instead of writing. A private verdict goes, readable by your account alone, to `~/.abcd.noindex/ideas/<root-sha>/`, with no decision-log line. A public one goes to `.abcd/development/research/ideas/<root-sha>/`, with its `DECISIONS.md` pointer. `/abcd:ideate` asks the question before its first leg.

**Each finding in a release receipt is fixed, invalid or deferred, and a deferral needs its own record.** From release-gate manifest `schemaVersion` 2, a finding in a release review receipt is `fixed`, `invalid` or `deferred` and nothing else. A deferred finding names its own open issue record in a `record` field. A missing, closed, symlinked or shared record is refused, in CI and in `abcd launch receipts` alike.

**The guard blocks stopping whatever holds a port or a file, as it blocks stopping by name.** It has two new bundled blockers. `fuser-kill` covers `fuser -k` and `--kill`, in any flag cluster. `kill-by-holder` covers a kill handed what `lsof` or `fuser` prints, through a substitution, `xargs` or a shell string. Each blocker names the alternative: the recorded pid or your own process group, or, for a peer's process, messaging that session or asking the person. Looking stays allowed (`lsof -i`, `fuser` without `-k`).

**The guard blocks `kill-port` and sees through package runners.** `kill-port <port>` now blocks as stopping by holder does, under a new `kill-port` entry that names the same alternatives. `npx`, `npm exec` (and `npm x`), `pnpm dlx` and `yarn dlx` are read as wrappers whose first operand is the program, with any version spec read off the name. So a blocked command run behind a package runner is blocked too.

**RepoPrompt over MCP as an opt-in reviewer route.** With `oracle.review = rp` in the repository's or the machine's abcd configuration, a `build` lane sends its ruthless and security reviews to RepoPrompt over MCP and records each verdict as it records any validator's. When RepoPrompt is unreachable, the host's own agent runs the review and the receipt says that the review fell back and why. Without the setting nothing changes, and abcd never spawns, installs or configures RepoPrompt.
`abcd peers` skips the embargo store without reading it and counts it without a path. A private record kept there, title included, is no longer shown to every local session that runs `abcd peers`.

Deleting the release-gate manifest no longer silently reverts `record-lint --release-gate` to its pre-manifest rules. The gate now refuses a release whose tree has no manifest when an older release tag's tree had one. A repository whose releases never had the manifest keeps the pre-manifest rules.

`abcd build next` refuses, at the pick stage with exit 2, any run count you name that differs from a live series' own, `--max 1` included. Before, it continued the series. An explicit `--max 0` is now refused with exit 2 and the same words as a negative count (a run count is 1 or more). A call that names no count still continues the series.

The `/abcd:build` command page lists all four refusals the pick commit's worktree stage can raise, each with its cause and what to do: a missing git identity, the intent no longer planned in the lane's worktree, a lane branch whose first commit is not the pick's, and a worktree dirty with other changes.

An unknown flag no longer blames a stale binary when the binary is not stale. A dev build run from a source checkout through `go run` is told that the plugin surface documents the flag and this build lacks it, with no `abcd update` advice; only a release-stamped copy still gets that advice. The note also matches only a fenced synopsis line that invokes exactly the command typed, so a flag mentioned in prose or under another sub-verb gets the plain unknown-flag refusal.

**`abcd guard` judges a command behind an append or subscript assignment.** `NAME+=`, `NAME[SUB]=` and `NAME[SUB]+=` are read as assignment prefixes wherever `NAME=` is, as bash and zsh read them, so `FOO+=x rm -rf /` is judged as the `rm` it runs and blocks, while ordinary lines such as `FOO+=x echo hi` stay allowed.

**abcd's home folder is your account's alone.** Before any command runs, abcd narrows an existing home folder it owns that other accounts could list or read to the owner only, and does the same for each lane worktree it adds; it never follows a symlink and never changes a folder another account owns. New home and store folders were already created owner-only.

**`abcd update` and `abcd ahoy install` verify a release binary's signed build provenance, not only the release page's checksums.** Before swapping or promoting a binary, abcd checks the release's SLSA provenance in process, held to abcd's own release workflow, so a binary and checksum list replaced together on the release page is refused; any failure, offline included, refuses and names the by-hand install. On a cold cache, `ahoy install` adopts an existing PATH copy only after the same check on the copy's own bytes, and a copy that fails or cannot be checked ends the run partial with the `gh attestation verify` command for that file.

**The plugin's first-run bootstrap and the site's install script verify the download with `gh attestation verify` when `gh` is available.** A failed verification refuses the install; with `gh` absent, too old for the command or not signed in, they install on the checksum alone with a warning naming why and the check to run by hand. The install one-liners in the README and the install guide carry the same step.

**A cached abcd release older than the newest one this machine has installed is refused.** The bootstrap, `abcd update` and the site's install script record a newest-release mark in abcd's home folder, the cache attestation names the release it vouches for, and `ahoy install` and the bootstrap refuse a cached release older than the mark; a withdrawn release is refused naming `abcd update <tag>`, the one way to lower the mark. A failed attestation write removes the old attestation instead of leaving it in place.
**The site's install script ends by reporting the installed version** through `abcd --version`, instead of an error from a `version` command abcd does not have.

**abcd reads its settings from a group-writable home folder only when that group is its owner's alone.** A folder its group can write is refused unless the group's only member is the owner, and refused whenever the members cannot be read, as on macOS or where accounts come from a network directory service. The refusal names the repair: `chmod g-w`, or `chmod go-w` when every account can write it.

**The status line's trust check judges every link in a chain.** Each hop of the recorded entry's link chain is judged where it sits, so a link inside the working tree, in a directory its group or other accounts can write, or in another account's directory is refused, as is a chain of more than four links.

**A rule from a user or repository override cannot render as a heading.** Each override rule body is rendered inside a code fence under its bullet, longer than any fence in the body, so no markdown in it renders for a reader that shows the injected rules as markdown; bundled rules keep their markdown.
**The release cut refuses another account's home path in the changelog or the release page**, naming the kind and the line but never the path; usernames stay allowed.

**A release scan exclusion that matches no file is named.** The dry run, the ship report and the cut's precheck warn on every declared exclusion fragment that matched nothing, so a typo or a fragment left behind by a rename is seen, and refuse under `strict_warnings`.

**`abcd guard` follows a value the same line assigns and then uses.** A pid list a search printed into a variable or a file and then killed, a pid list a `grep` or `awk` filter takes from a `ps` listing, a stream path in a variable a shell reads, text a variable holds that a string runs, and `pkill` or `killall` named through a variable are each judged as what they carry. A variable the line did not set reads as before, so `kill "$pid"`, `ps -o pid= -p N | xargs kill`, a recorded pid file and `"$GO" build` stay allowed.

**`abcd guard` refuses a script a line downloads or writes and then runs.** A file saved from `curl` or `wget` and then run, sourced or fed to a shell on the same line is refused as reading a stream, and a `source` or `.` of a file the line writes is refused even when that file does not exist yet.

**`abcd guard` reads a script found through an extended `PATH`.** After `PATH=dir:$PATH`, `export PATH="dir:$PATH"` or `PATH+=:dir`, the search walks the value entry by entry, so a sourced file in `dir` is judged; `export PATH="$HOME/bin:$PATH"` on its own stays allowed.

**`abcd guard` reads the file zsh would run.** zsh's `path` array is read as `PATH`, a zsh `source` of a bare name looks in the working directory first, and where the shell is not known both readings are judged; a variable the line sets without `export` is read as handed down to a child shell unless the line takes the export away.

**`abcd guard` follows `cd` and `pushd` into the directory the shell enters.** A bare `pushd` swaps to the directory the line's own `pushd` left, and leaves the directory unknown, never home, where the line did not set the stack; bash's `cd a b c` enters `a`; and zsh's `cd -x` enters a directory named `-x` where one exists. The scripts that follow are read there.

**`abcd guard` allows two everyday lines it blocked.** After `unset CDPATH`, a `cd name` is read with no `CDPATH` search, and zsh's `fpath=(dir $fpath); autoload -Uz compinit` and `fpath+=(dir)` idioms read `$fpath` as the account's own directories; a fixed directory holding a hazard still blocks.

**The implement loop keeps a repository's own git settings wherever your own git would.** Lane worktrees and restarts read your global and system git config, so a Git LFS repository's lanes hold the real files rather than pointer text; the pick commit and the sync merge run the repository's hooks, commit signing and merge drivers; a lane's checkout runs its post-checkout hook under its own sixty-minute bound, and a restart's reset runs its hooks. A sync the repository refuses before merging is refused with git's reason.

**A lane branch another checkout stands on is protected on a case-folding filesystem.** Landing or discarding a lane compares branch names without regard to case where the filesystem folds case, as macOS does by default, so a run naming `build/Lane-1` refuses to delete `build/lane-1` from under a worktree that has it checked out.
**`abcd build` and `abcd drain` start on time even when a runner's quota report ignores its deadline.** The start's quota query returns at the caller's deadline whatever the runner does.

**The planning interview's change guard pins each submodule's git pointers before git runs.** A changed `commondir` in a submodule's git directory, a rewritten `.git` pointer in a submodule's path, and the pointer of a submodule added since the first reading are each refused before git reads through them.

**abcd refuses a hand-edited run file that carries hidden characters.** A series, run state, drain state or lane receipt whose stored pace settings, hand-back or judgement text, receipt model or resolution text holds a control, bidirectional or zero-width character is refused when read, without echoing the value, so none reaches the `--json` output of `build next`, `drain`, `implement record` or `implement status`.

**Repository and tool text on abcd's `--json` output is masked.** Control, bidirectional and zero-width characters are masked in a run's state where it is stored and where it is read, in spec step titles and the pull-request titles built from them, in the run log's outage spans and every `implement report` field, in a runner's reported model, in issue-record validation errors, and in the reasons, titles and records `drain`, `capture list` and `capture status` show; the records themselves are left as written.

**abcd's terminal-safe mask covers more invisible characters.** Unicode tag characters, the interlinear annotation marks, the Mongolian vowel separator and the combining grapheme joiner are masked wherever abcd masks text, and refused wherever it refuses hidden characters.

**record-lint's agent-contract check closes two ways around a prompt version bump.** A prompt under `agents/` that is a symlink, or an `agents` directory that is or lies under one, is reported naming the path; and only a higher `prompt_version` counts as a bump, so moving a prompt back to an older version is reported naming both.

**`abcd implement load --wait` holds across every account on the machine.** It reads the process table and stays shut while any account's `make preflight`, an earlier waiter or a race test run is live, then waits a random 15 to 60 seconds and checks again before opening; no file is shared between accounts. abcd's own `make preflight` runs its test stages behind this gate, with test parallelism sized to the cores and the current load.

**The `/abcd:` menu lists the commands people use.** Commands only agents run, such as the guard that judges a shell command, are hidden from the menu and keep their names; typed in full, the host says to ask the agent, which still runs them. The menu holds 15 commands where it held 35, `abcd --help` lists the same commands for a person, and `abcd --help --agent` lists every verb with the page an agent reads next.

**Breaking: seven commands are merged or retired, with no alias.** `abcd source` and `abcd memory`, with the `/abcd:source`, `/abcd:memory`, `/abcd:consult` and `/abcd:ingest` pages, merge into `abcd library` (`init`, `add`, `declassify`, `ledger`, `sync-banlist`, `cite-check`, `ingest`, `ask` and `lint`), whose `add` asks a source's class at a terminal when none is given; `abcd changelog` is gone, and `abcd launch --dry-run` previews the release cut instead; `/abcd:prepare-this-repo` folds into `/abcd:ahoy install`; and the `/abcd:version` page retires, while the board shows the installed version and `abcd --version` still answers. A script or habit that calls an old name stops working: call the new one.

**`abcd build next` picks the readiest planned intent itself, and writes down why.** It considers every planned intent that passes every check `abcd build <itd-N>` runs, scores each on its own record (how clear its acceptance criteria are, whether its spec names the tests, how few packages it touches), takes the readiest, oldest among equals, and commits onto that intent a grounds entry naming every candidate, why each lost and what would show the pick wrong, as the lane's first commit. It makes one pick per run; `--max <n>` or `--until-empty` keeps it going. A spec gains a `## Footprint` section the score reads.

**A spec lists its steps, and `abcd build` lands them one at a time.** A spec's `## Steps` section, seeded empty by `abcd intent plan`, is built as one lane and one pull request per step, in order, and a step runs beside earlier ones only when its plan says so; a spec with no steps is one step. A step that does not fit the cut leaves the unfinished steps in the remainder spec `spec close --remainder` mints.

**An autonomous run keeps a pace it was never told.** A run started with `abcd build` or `abcd drain` follows a working window, a pause after it and a ceiling on lanes and validators alive at once, layered flag over repository over machine over the bundled default of 120 minutes of work, no pause and two lanes, and the run record names the layer that applied. `--pace <work-minutes>/<pause-minutes>` and `--sub-agents <n>` set them for one run. A pause is a time written into the run's state file, and an invocation before it refuses, naming it. Where a runner reports its remaining quota, a run whose estimate exceeds it refuses to start; a rate-limit response checkpoints the lane and ends the window early.

**Setup asks whether abcd keeps parts of the README current, and which.** `abcd ahoy install` asks the owner, and on a yes offers the parts it can read from the project itself, each in its own marked place: a line naming the licence, links to files such as the changelog, contributing guide and security policy, a table of contents and, for a project declared public, the forge's live release and build badges, with a managed-with-abcd badge off unless turned on. `--readme-parts <list>|none` answers without the questions. Each setup run rewrites the chosen parts; abcd never writes the title or the owner's own words, reports and leaves a part edited by hand, and creates a README holding only the chosen parts where none exists.

**`abcd implement load --wait -- <command>` waits for capacity before it runs a command.** One waiter judges race runs by their arguments with its own ancestry excluded, waits for the machine's load to fall below a per-machine limit, and admits one waiter at a time through a machine-wide hold. It exits with the command's code, or 128 plus the signal number when a signal killed the command (143 for SIGTERM). The LOAD rule domain teaches it in place of hand-written wait loops.

**An implement run stops when the repository's git settings change under it.** The run's first check records a fingerprint of every repository-level git setting that can name a program (filters, hooks, diff and merge drivers, signing programs and remote addresses among them), the hooks directory and each lane worktree's own settings. Every later step, discard, restart and rate-limit checkpoint compares it first and stops, naming the changed keys and files but never a value, so a filter planted in a lane never runs. `abcd implement step --accept-config-change` records the settings as they stand once a person has looked.

**Staged transcripts of a repository that no longer exists can be discarded.** The session-start report gives such a pile its own line naming the repository, its root commit and its size, with the commands to list and discard it; `abcd history staged` and `abcd history discard` take `--root-sha` and reach the user-level store with no checkout, and `staged --all-repos` marks the row ORPHANED. Discarding keeps its per-file `--yes`, and nothing is deleted automatically.

**`abcd guard` refuses an `rm` whose operand starts with a variable that can be empty, followed by `/`.** `rm -f "$VAR"/*` is refused with `"${VAR:?}"/...` or a literal path as the form to run instead, and the SHELL rule domain teaches it. Inside a double-quoted `sh -c` string the guarded form is allowed, while an alternative or an escaped default that expands to nothing there is refused; a guard nested in a default is read, and arithmetic expansion stays allowed.

**`abcd guard` reads the script the shell actually runs.** A `..` in a script path resolves physically, as the kernel does, and `cd -P` records the physical directory; a `source` command's own `PATH` prefix is the path its search reads; and a `cd` that searches `CDPATH` enters the one directory holding its operand when exactly one exists, and otherwise refuses, its reason saying whether the line set `CDPATH` or the environment exported it.

**`abcd guard` follows a `cd` the way both bash and zsh read it.** zsh's `-q` and `-s` and `pushd -n` are read as options, and where the two shells read a `cd` or `pushd` differently (a second operand, or an option word one or neither shell takes), the scripts after it are read in every directory either reading enters, and a hazard in any of them blocks.

**`abcd guard` reads two ways zsh runs code from a file.** A process substitution spelled `=(...)` is read as a stream, as `<(...)` is, so sourcing or running one is refused; and `autoload`, `functions -u` and `typeset -fu` are read as loading a function file, found through the `FPATH` or `fpath` the line sets and judged, with a name, option or directory the line does not fix refused as an unread script.

**`abcd guard` refuses a `BASH_ENV` or `ENV` value the shell would expand.** A value holding a dollar sign or a backquote is refused as an unread script, both where a shell is handed it and where a script run directly reads `BASH_ENV`, because the shell expands the value before it opens the file.

**An abcd question is judged on its own label.** The question check sets whose answer is awaited from the question's chip (Product for the product thinker, Tech and Setup for the facilitator) and never refuses a labelled question on the mode, which returns to managed when the answer comes back. A refusal for another fault lists only the parts that refuse it, with a rows overrun noted as never refusing on its own; and when git will not name the repository root, the check says so on stderr and exits 1 instead of letting the question through without a word.

**READY means the build will start.** `abcd intent ready`, the closing verdict of `abcd intent interview`, `abcd itd-N` and the `abcd spc-N` page run the build's open-questions check, so an intent whose `## Open Questions` still lists an unanswered item reads NOT READY, and its next move names the questions and the planning interview instead of saying to implement.

**The implement loop no longer waits in silence on a pull request that cannot merge.** The land stage reads the pull request's mergeability from the forge and refuses a conflicting one, naming the files a driver-free merge conflicts in and the merge drivers the forge ignores, with a hand merge as the remedy. Each drain move finishes landing every lane whose pushed head is on the default branch, removing its worktree and branch.

**Restarting or discarding a lane touches only that lane.** `abcd implement step --discard` and a hand-back's discard refuse, before removing anything, when another checkout has the lane's branch checked out, naming it. A restart and a rate-limit checkpoint copy aside only a receipt file inside the lane's own directory and refuse anything else with nothing changed; a checkpoint whose save-aside is refused marks the await, so `abcd implement step --restart <lane>` re-tells it, a validator's included; and a checkpoint leaves alone an await a restart has already re-told.

**`abcd build` and `abcd drain` cannot hang on the start's quota query.** It runs under a two-minute deadline, and its error reaches the budget row and the run record with the home directory redacted.

**The implement loop's sync merge works on git older than 2.44.** Its built-in merge passes the histogram diff and its labels only on git 2.44 or later, so a merge on Apple Git 2.39.5 no longer fails on an option it does not know, and still no repository merge driver starts.
**The implement loop's refusal of a base without AGENTS.md names `/abcd:ahoy install`**, which sets one up, instead of a command that does not exist.

**The status board's Now list titles a run started for an issue.** Its rows carry the issue's one-line summary prefixed `issue:`, and a lane leaves the list once its branch is gone or has landed on the default branch.

**A record's file name stays within the Windows path limit.** Every minted slug is cut at 40 characters, and every record minted before the cap is renamed to it, with ids unchanged and every link rewritten; the release cut keys a record on its id within its folder, so a renamed record is neither added nor removed.

**Surprise, admission, disposition and reframe records draw a new id on a clash.** A minted id that lands on an existing record is drawn again, as issue ids are, instead of refusing the write when two records are minted in the same second.

**A cold reading's excluded sections cannot travel under a variant heading.** A heading differing only in case is redacted, and headings match only when they render alike; a heading inside an HTML block, or one spelled with a lookalike character such as a Cyrillic letter, is refused rather than passed into the bundle.

**A principle link with parentheses in its address is read whole.** Principle statement links unwrap through the shared CommonMark link scanner, so an address such as `Audit_(finance)`, an escaped parenthesis, an angle-bracket address or a title no longer leaves a fragment in the reading bundle.

**The README contents part links the anchors the forge renders.** Anchors are built from a heading's rendered text, with character references decoded and inline HTML dropped; a heading inside an open HTML block is not listed; code spans are read once; and a heading with an emoji shortcode, with any later heading whose anchor it could shift, is listed without a link and named in a note. A README the parts would grow past setup's 1 MiB cap is refused, naming the cap, and left unchanged.

**A broken documentation check no longer passes in silence.** Bare `abcd lint` raises a target's refusal as an error finding and exits 2, so a docs-lint root naming a retired file fails instead of being skipped; `abcd ahoy` reports each missing root as the gap `docs_lint.root_missing`; and `ahoy install` seeds `.abcd/docs-lint.json` with `docs` and `README.md` only where they exist.

**The hooks advice no longer shadows a global hooks dispatcher.** The pre-commit and prepare-commit-msg hooks `ahoy install` scaffolds, abcd's contributing guide and its commit-msg hook give the three-way `core.hooksPath` advice: set it when unarmed, have a foreign dispatcher call `.githooks/`, and do nothing when armed.

**The `.gitignore` block `ahoy install` writes has a plain ASCII comment line**, so a repository whose writing rules ban non-ASCII no longer fails on a line it cannot edit; a block carrying the old comment still reads as no drift.

**abcd refuses a home directory inside a working tree as its machine layer.** A `$HOME` at or below a checkout is not read as the machine's abcd configuration or credential home unless it is the account's own home, as the account database names it and never as the environment says; the machine layer then reads as absent, with a note naming the refusal.

**The macOS keychain home refuses a value too long for the `security` tool before writing it.** Measured on a Mac, the longest value that round-trips is 2001 bytes; a longer one is refused naming the limit and pointing at the abcd home, where it used to fail with nothing stored.

**A refused release cut names its uncommitted open records.** An issue record under `open/` that differs from HEAD gets a refusal entry of its own beside any unfixed or deleted finding, the findings line counts them, and `commands/launch.md` and the brief say the unfixed-finding refusal covers them.

**`exclude_path_fragments` matches whole path segments.** A fragment's segments must appear in order in the path, a fragment ending in `/` names a directory, a dot-led fragment with no slash also matches the end of a file name, and a single-character fragment is a configuration fault that makes the scanner unavailable, so the launch refuses rather than drop files from its scan.

**record-lint's agent-contract check compares the `prompt_version` itself.** It reads the frontmatter value on both sides of the range, so an instruction edit under `agents/` no longer passes on an added body line or a trailing space.

**The disembark probe grounds the invariants, naming and personas sections in their own brief files**, as it does open questions and trade-offs, and the pack's per-section file prints a partial section's reason as `Why partial:`.

**A git lookup with no deadline waits for git's answer on a loaded machine.** The site build's root lookup and the root-commit lookup no longer fail when git's output is slow to arrive; under a deadline a miss is retried once and then reported as a timeout, never as no root commit.

**Stopping the dashboard tells a gone server from a slow read.** On Linux a process that exits during the read counts as gone; on macOS a `ps` killed by its own timeout is an error, so stopping no longer takes a live server for stale and forgets it.

**The issue-resolution gate names a near-miss declaration.** A `Refs:` or `Resolves:` line naming an issue beside an intent, ADR or spec id is refused with its fix: put the issue ids on a line of their own.

**abcd's own CI no longer stalls its merge queue.** The macOS suite runs once per change, in the queue and in one race-enabled pass, and reports from an ubuntu runner on a pull request; CI no longer reruns on a push to `main` and checks the default branch nightly; superseded merge-queue runs are cancelled; and the queue's check timeout is 90 minutes.
abcd's tests create their bare repositories with git's background maintenance off, so a test's cleanup no longer fails on a directory git is still writing.

**Autonomous runs wait out a lost connection.** When the network or the model service drops during an `abcd implement` run, lanes carry on with offline work and wait at the steps that need the lost service on one probe shared by the machine and recorded in the run state, retried at 1, 5 and 10 minutes and then hourly for up to 8 hours, each probe testing only what failed. If the service has not returned by then, the run stops every step, reports what was done and what is left, and notifies once. A usage or rate limit is reported as it is and never waited out as an outage. `abcd implement step --restart <lane-id>` saves a dead or yielded lane's uncommitted edits aside for review and restarts it from its last commit.

**`abcd guard` reads a script a shell will run before it judges the command.** A script operand, a `source` operand, a startup file named by `BASH_ENV`, `ENV`, `--rcfile` or `--init-file`, the startup files a shell reads under an assigned `HOME` or `ZDOTDIR`, and a file redirected into a shell's standard input are now read and judged against the registry like the command itself. A script written earlier on the same line is refused, a startup file given as a process substitution is refused as a stream, and the stream refusal no longer suggests running an unread file instead.

**`abcd guard` judges the commands bash takes from its environment.** Command substitutions in a `PS0`, `PS1`, `PS2` or `PS4` value and a `PROMPT_COMMAND` value are judged wherever the line assigns them, and the body of a function exported to bash through `env` or `sudo` is judged with the inline rules. `env` and `sudo` now treat every `NAME=value` operand before the command as an assignment, as they apply it.

**`abcd guard` judges the command string given to `trap`.** A `trap` action, and the callback of `mapfile` or `readarray -C`, is read the way `eval`'s arguments are, so a blocked command there now blocks. The reset and list forms, such as `trap - EXIT`, carry no command and stay allowed.

**`abcd guard` judges the body of a `function name { ... }` definition.** A blocked command inside a function written with the `function` keyword now blocks, as it already did in the `name() { ... }` form, where it used to only warn and so ran. zsh's `repeat COUNT` is stepped over the same way.

**The secret scanner counts a file as text only when the whole file is text.** It used to decide from the first 8 KiB. A file with a NUL byte or invalid UTF-8 anywhere is now Unscanned with its reason, so the launch gate refuses it instead of counting it as scanned.

**The secret scanner decodes a JSON escape stacked on a percent encoding.** Each decoder now also runs over the other's output, in both orders, with every hit mapped back to the raw line, so a token or home path encoded both ways is found, refused by the launch gate and redacted.

**The secret scanner scans the bytes a compressed PNG chunk carries after its zlib stream.** In zTXt, iTXt, iCCP and IDAT chunks that tail is now decoded and scanned, where the image used to count as fully decoded with it unread.

**The secret scanner scans the whole of a tar archive's extension headers.** A GNU long-name or long-link body is covered past its first NUL, a PAX header body is covered whole, and each body's padding must be zero, where the archive used to count as fully decoded with part of those bodies unread.

**A skip fragment no longer exempts files from the launch scan without saying so.** A file that `skip_path_fragments` in `.abcd/config/pii.json` alone sends to byte-only scanning is now Unscanned with its reason, so the launch refuses and names it, unless its extension or name is on the reviewed skip lists. A cut that relied on such a fragment refuses until the path is excluded on purpose: the new `exclude_path_fragments` field takes a fragment with a required reason, and those files are reported as excluded by choice and never counted as scanned.

**abcd's git reads fetch nothing missing from a partial clone.** abcd sets `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`, so on git 2.44 or later reading a missing object is an error and starts no configured transport.
