Git older than 2.44 ignores that variable (Apple's Command Line Tools ship 2.39), so there abcd refuses, before git starts and naming the 2.44 floor, every object-reading git command in a repository that declares a partial clone or a promisor remote, `check-ignore`, `config --blob` and most `ls-files` forms included. A repository with no promisor remote reads as before.

**The launch dirty check runs no content filter the repository names.** It blanks every clean, smudge and process filter before its diff against HEAD, so a checkout's filter program neither runs nor decides what reads as clean, and a required filter fails the check closed. abcd's filter-free working-tree reads (status, the launch and intent-consistency dirty checks, the release-receipts status) also pass `--ignore-submodules=dirty`, so no filter a submodule's own config names runs; a moved submodule pointer still reads as a change.

**Read-only `git log` and `git show` calls start no signing program.** Every git command abcd runs in isolation pins `log.showSignature=false`, so reading a signed commit during a probe such as `abcd disembark probe`, the site history or the decisions-append check no longer starts the repository's `gpg.program`.

**record-lint's agent-contract bump check runs no diff program the repository names.** Its diffs pass `--no-ext-diff` and `--no-textconv` and blank the repository's content filters first, so no `diff.external`, diff driver command, textconv or clean filter runs or writes the text the check reads for a `prompt_version` bump.

**A patch diff abcd runs starts no diff inside a submodule.** Every git command abcd runs in isolation pins `diff.submodule=short`, so record-lint's decisions-append and agent-contract diffs show a moved submodule as its pointer change and no submodule's own `diff.external` or textconv runs.

**The implement loop's pick commit and sync merge start no signing program, automatic gc or maintenance.** They run with `commit.gpgsign=false`, `gc.auto=0`, `maintenance.auto=false` and `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`, so no `gpg.program`, `gpg.ssh.program` or `gpg.ssh.defaultKeyCommand` starts and a merge in a partial clone fetches nothing; the commit is still made and content filters still run.

**The implement loop's lane sync merge runs no merge program the repository names.** Every configured merge driver, and `merge.default`, is replaced with git's built-in text merge for that merge, so the result is git's own.

**The implement loop refuses a worktree path it did not derive.** The land, implement and validate stages and both worktree discards now check the run state's worktree path as the brief stage does, and refuse before anything is created, run or removed at a path the loop did not derive.

**abcd refuses a repository root that `core.worktree` points above the checkout.** A root is accepted only when its `.git` is the git directory git found, or a gitfile naming it, so `abcd decide`, intent, spec, capture and memory writes can no longer land in an ancestor directory.

**`abcd ahoy` reports an ignored `~/.abcd.noindex/filter-roots` file.** A filter-roots file that fails its ownership, mode or symlink checks is still ignored, but `abcd ahoy` now reports it from any folder as the machine-scope gap `filter_roots.ignored`, naming the check it failed, so content filters no longer switch off for a listed checkout with no notice.

**`abcd dashboard start` starts when one Tailscale address cannot be reached.** Start now drops a Tailscale address its self-check cannot connect to, naming it and the reason in the start line and `--json`, and serves on the addresses that answered; it refuses only when none does. On a Mac whose Tailscale could not reach its own IPv6 address, the dashboard used to stop and could not be opened from any device.

**abcd is built with Go 1.26.9.** The toolchain moves from Go 1.26.7, picking up the standard library's fixes for vulnerabilities in packages abcd reaches, among them `net/http` and the `html/template` that renders the dashboard page; `govulncheck` reports no reachable vulnerability.

**The launch, prepare-this-repo and implement docs match the code.** `commands/launch.md` and the `--allow-dirty` help name the findings gate's refusal of records still in `open/` (and the help, the cut's refusal of uncommitted records); prepare-this-repo sets the hooks path only when it is unarmed and names `.abcd/record-lint.json`; the `implement step --discard` help lists its steps in the order the code runs them.

**`abcd intent edge` links one intent to another.** `abcd intent edge <itd-N>` adds and removes an intent's `blocked_by` and `builds_on` edges with `--blocked-by`, `--unblock`, `--builds-on` and `--drop-builds-on`, as `capture link` does for issues, so the build gate's blocked check no longer depends on hand-typed edges. It refuses an id no intent store holds, an edge from an intent to itself, and removing an edge that is not there, and writes nothing when it refuses.

**A question that is only too long is shown, with a note to the agent.** When the question guard's only finding is the rows limit, the question now reaches the person and the agent is told which tabs ran over and by how much. A new `abcd:question-drafter` agent drafts abcd's questions so they fit, counting rows as the check does. The guard hook also refuses through the host's JSON deny, so a refused command no longer echoes the hook's command line before the guard's message.

**`abcd ahoy install` shows what each approval will write.** Each category approval now lists the changes it would apply, asks in plain words, and its yes option says how many changes it writes. Before this, each approval was a single line such as "Apply conventions-file changes?" whose yes option pointed at text above that did not exist. The question check now refuses any question whose yes option points at text above when no such text is given.

**A refused `abcd ahoy install` exits 2.** The install refuses on a symlinked `.abcd`, a stale binary or the retired `docs.target` value. In each case it still prints its result, then exits 2 where it used to exit 0, so a script can tell an install that wrote nothing from one that landed. `abcd ahoy remote apply` now exits 2 on a refusal too, where it used to exit 1, and an aborted apply still exits 1. A script that read a refused apply as exit 1 needs updating.

**`abcd ahoy` creates the committed tiers `abcd lint` requires.** An install that reported no gaps could leave out the shared working tier, so the newly adopted repository then failed `abcd lint` on `three-tier-layout`. `ahoy` now reads the same list of required tiers as the lint, detects a missing one and creates it, and seeds `.abcd/work/DECISIONS.md` with a header.

**A value flag on `abcd ahoy install` asks before it changes a saved setting.** A flag such as `--docs-target` that would change a saved setting now asks the config-change approval even when detection found no config gap. A decline drops the flag, saves nothing and names the flag; `--yes` or `approve.config-change` applies it. Before this, the setting was saved and `AGENTS.md` re-rendered even though every approval the run asked was declined.

**Banlist health reads the hooks path that git actually uses.** When a clone has no local `core.hooksPath`, banlist health now reads the global or system value, as git does, and reports the hooks path as armed, unarmed or foreign. A global dispatcher that chains to `.githooks/` is no longer reported as unarmed, and the status no longer tells you to arm the clone with a local override.

**`abcd lab` works in a repository that is not abcd.** In any other repository, `abcd lab preflight` reports the dual-binary group as not applicable and says why. Before this, every lab outside abcd halted at its first step, because the check required a `bin/abcd` that only abcd's own source can build. `abcd lab mint` also no longer tells such a repository to build `bin/abcd`.

**The bundled ROADMAP rules no longer teach phases and milestones.** A prompt about a roadmap, milestone or phase used to inject "each phase ends in a milestone" into managed repositories. It now injects the current statement: phases and milestones are retired, work is sequenced by dependencies and shelves, and the checkpoint is the derived release.

**The bundled INTENTS rules no longer limit personas to Alice, Bob and Carol.** The rule now teaches an open alphabetical sequence (Alice, Bob, Carol, Dave, and on) that a repository extends. It points at the repository's own persona roster for each persona's name and role, so adding a fourth persona no longer means overriding the whole rule.

**Ordinary prose that says "kill" no longer loads the SHELL rules.** A guard entry can now mark its command as an everyday verb, and such a command loads SHELL only with the flag or operand shape its pattern declares. A prompt such as "kill the feature flag" no longer injects the SHELL block, while `kill $(pgrep ...)` and `... | xargs kill` still do.

**The question guard's rows limit says what it counts.** When a question runs over the limit, the guard now reports the whole tab's rows, split into header and frame, question text, and options. The GRILL rule now says the twenty-four rows include the header, the host's frame, the question text, and every option's label and description, not the question text alone.

**The doc-fidelity coverage check runs even when no intent ships.** A release cut that ships only issue fixes, and a `spec close --remainder`, now refuse a verb, sub-verb or agent that no brief chapter names. Before this, both skipped the whole gate. A saved docs review is still required only where an intent ships.

**The release cut's findings gate sees uncommitted captures.** `launch ship` now refuses a working tree whose open issue records differ from HEAD, names every path, and offers no `--allow-dirty` waiver. Before this, a major or critical finding that had been captured but not committed was invisible to the gate.

**The OpenAI-compatible provider refuses a request too large for the model before sending it, where the server says how large that is.** Before each chat call, the adapter reads the service's model list. If the list gives the model's served size (vLLM's `max_model_len`), the adapter asks the same server's `/tokenize` for an exact count, and refuses only when that count plus `max_tokens` is over the size. The refusal names both numbers, where each came from, and a listed model that fits. Without both figures, the request is sent as before and the server's own refusal text is kept. The model-list read now happens on every call, with every provider. llama.cpp, LM Studio and Ollama publish their served size elsewhere and are not checked.

**The disembark probe reads the authored open-questions and tradeoffs brief files.** The open-questions and tradeoffs sections now also count as grounded from the repository's own `03-open-questions.md` and `04-tradeoffs.md`, and a stub counts as partial. Every partial verdict at every tier now gives its reason, shown as `why partial:`: what was found and what would ground it.
**`abcd report` accepts a plugin slash command in a field.** A field naming a command such as `/abcd:report` is no longer refused as a filesystem path; a real path still is.

**The `ahoy` page names both stray-hook gap ids.** A second abcd hook on the same event is reported as `harness.stray_hook.<Event>.<n>`, numbered from 2. `commands/ahoy.md` now says so, alongside `harness.stray_hook.<Event>`.

**A guard refusal reads as one short line.** Each hook's shell now lives in its own script under `hooks/`, and `hooks.json` runs it with a one-line command under fifty characters. When a hook refuses a call, the host's hook-error line now shows a short path followed by the hook's own message. Before this, it showed several thousand characters of inline shell, wrapped and cut at the terminal width, with the guard's message buried at the end.

**The interview's change guard can no longer be pointed at another git directory.** In a plain-Terminal interview, the guard's first reading of a run pins git's own directory and common directory, along with the two files that place them: a linked worktree's `.git` file and the git directory's `commondir`. If the interview's role rewrites either file during a turn, the guard names it as that turn's change and does not follow it. A reading in which git names directories other than the pinned ones is refused.

**A large file written into the working tree no longer holds an interview turn while it is hashed.** One reading of the change guard now hashes at most 2 GiB of what it owns. The paths git lists are sized before any of them is hashed, and a listing over the bound is refused with its largest path named. Git's own directory is counted as it is reached, and no file is hashed past its recorded size.

**Files git reads whole are now sized before git runs.** Before each reading, the change guard checks `HEAD`, `commondir`, `config.worktree`, `config`, `packed-refs` and `info/exclude` in the pinned directories against the same 2 GiB bound, and refuses past it with the largest named. An interview role that grows one of these files no longer holds the turn while git reads it.

**`launch ship` refuses an uncommitted record move.** The release derivation, not only the ingest, now refuses (`uncommitted-records`, exit 1) a working tree whose terminal record folders differ from HEAD, naming every path, instead of returning a plausible cut that silently leaves out a record whose close is not yet committed; `abcd changelog` carries the same refusal.

**`abcd ahoy` names an abcd hook wired outside the plugin.** It reports every hook in the harness's user settings that runs abcd, and an abcd status line whose binary fails the trust checks, naming the file, the entry and the remedy, and session start names such an entry in one line, so a stale build that keeps recreating the old `~/.abcd` home is found rather than hunted down by hand; abcd never edits that file to remove a hook.

**The printed rename repair reaches every worktree.** The repair line abcd prints and documents is now one `find` that runs `git worktree repair` at each worktree's `.git` file at any depth, so a worktree named with a slash (such as `docs/<name>`) is relinked instead of left pointing at the old home; it says a `repair: gitdir incorrect` line is a link fixed, and `abcd ahoy` reports each store worktree still unlinked as `store.worktree_unlinked` with that worktree's own repair line.

**`dashboard start` never signals a server that has already exited.** A server that exits at once gets the exit grace instead of being treated as stuck when its configuration write fails, and start reaps the server itself, so it never kills a process group whose number may by then belong to another program.

**The status line is the one entry abcd writes in the harness's user settings, and only on a yes.** `abcd ahoy install` shows that entry's before and after and writes it only after an explicit yes, keeps a copy (the newest 10), reads the file back and restores it on a mismatch, wires only the recorded trusted PATH install and never records abcd's own verb as the previous command; the status verb writes nothing and is time-bounded, and uninstall restores the previous status line.

**An AI-written interview role can no longer stall the change guard with a huge tree outside the checkout.** What one reading reads outside what it owns, the targets of the links it follows and a hooks directory `core.hooksPath` names outside the tree alike, is held to 1,024 entries and 64 MiB in all, and a reading past it is refused promptly, naming the link or the configured `core.hooksPath` value, where the guard used to hash for minutes before failing closed.

**Breaking: abcd's home folder is now `~/.abcd.noindex`, and abcd stops until you rename the old one.** On a Mac the desktop search indexer passes over that name, so a working copy, a run log or a transcript kept there sets off no indexing burst; a new install starts with it, and abcd never touches the computer's own search settings. While `~/.abcd` stands, every abcd command, every hook and the status line stops before writing anything and names the one command to run. In an agent session the safety check then blocks every command, the rename included, so run `mv ~/.abcd ~/.abcd.noindex` in a plain Terminal window, then the worktree repair line the stop prints, which reconnects the git worktrees kept in the folder before anything prunes them. With both folders present abcd stops, names both and moves neither. A managed project's conventions block keeps naming the old paths until `abcd ahoy install` runs in it again, and a script of your own that names `~/.abcd/` is yours to change: a link from the old name does not keep it working, because abcd takes any entry at the old name for the old folder and stops. See docs/how-to/upgrade-to-v0.13.0.md.

**Breaking: AGENTS.md is the one conventions file abcd writes.** Setup and embark write AGENTS.md and no separate copy for any tool, and prepare-this-repo scaffolds none. A project whose saved `docs.target` is `claude_md` or `both` stops at setup before writing anything, and abcd names the one setting to change (`abcd ahoy install --docs-target agents_md`, or `skip` for no block); the project still reads as managed and still uninstalls cleanly. An existing tool's file that holds your own words is left exactly as it is, with a loud warning that AGENTS.md stays hidden until you move those words across and remove the file; a file that only repeats or links to AGENTS.md is offered for removal and goes only on a yes. Setup also warns when an older version of your agent tool, or a conventions file in a folder above the project, would hide AGENTS.md. See docs/how-to/upgrade-to-v0.13.0.md.

**Breaking: a repository's `.abcd/config.json` can no longer hand a role to a command-line runner on your key.** Only a personal route, the machine's own configuration or your own invocation, sends a role to the `claude` or `opencode` runner; a repository's `roles.<role>.runner` is skipped with a note naming the file, the key and the machine's file, and the role runs on the host as if unrouted. To keep a runner route, set it in your machine's configuration. The `opencode` runner also launches with project configuration, other tools' instruction files and external skills switched off beside `--pure`, so a repository's instructions, settings, agents and skills no longer reach the run. See docs/how-to/upgrade-to-v0.13.0.md.

**Every question an abcd agent puts to a person is asked one at a time, in plain language.** A planning interview, a decomposition routing, a grill or any stop for a verdict asks one thing at a time, quotes the thing being decided in full, carries one concrete example of what each answer would mean, and offers options that widen rather than recommend: no starred default, no recommended label, and the way to decide later always offered. Deferral is recorded as an answer, and silence is never consent. The rule ships as a bundled rule domain, GRILL, so a session that never read the protocol follows it from its first prompt.

**Every question abcd asks is built the same way, and a badly built one is refused before it reaches you.** Each carries a short label saying who it is for and which question it is ("Product Q2"), the thing being decided quoted in full in paragraphs and lists, one plain question, two to four options each with a label of a few words and a sentence or two on what choosing it means, and always a way to decide later. Nothing you need lives only in a side preview. A question with a starred or "(Recommended)" option, a side preview, or a part over its limit is refused naming the part and the limit, so it is asked again properly, and one that passes reads at 80 columns without scrolling.

**Connecting a model service from inside your coding session looks up the details and offers the choices.** abcd asks for the service's address and, on a yes, looks up the models it offers, with no key sent; it suggests the models you already use through other connections and narrows the full list as you type part of a name, and a service that lists no models asks for the name and says why. It then prints one command, with every file that command will write, to paste into a terminal: nothing is set up from inside the session. Where the service needs the key before it lists its models, that terminal step reads the key with the typing hidden, lets you pick a model, checks the pick with a real answer, and only then saves anything.

Commits the implement loop composes from the run's records, the pick commit and the sync merge, now declare `Assisted-by: abcd:<version>` (the release version, or `dev`) instead of `Assisted-by: None`; the attribution gate and the commit hook accept it as a third form and refuse a malformed abcd label.

The implement loop arms auto-merge only where an active ruleset on the default branch requires a person's approval, an approving review or a code-owner review with an owner named; otherwise the pull request is left open for a person and never armed later, so agent-written code no longer merges on CI alone. CODEOWNERS is read as the forge reads it: only the first file found (`.github/`, the root, `docs/`), and a line counts only when an owner follows its pattern.

The plain-Terminal interview's guard now stops the interview when a role writes through a linked `.git/hooks`, `.git/info` or `.git/config`, a linked hook or a submodule's linked hooks, reading each link where it leads; and when a role registers a worktree, plants a push receipt in another worktree, or repoints a sibling worktree's `commondir` or `gitdir`, naming the path.

The secret scanner's bundled patterns now know OpenRouter keys (`sk-or-v1-`), OpenAI's legacy key shape and its `sk-admin-` admin keys, as hard failures, and a plain `sk-` key of 32 or more letters and digits as a warning, so every redactor masks it and the guided connect refuses one typed where a model name belongs, while lint and the launch scan do not fail a committed file on it.

A failed model-service call's error quotes the service's answer only when it arrived whole; one cut off by the wait, the 16 KiB size bound or a read error is reported by its status alone and named as cut off, so the error can no longer carry the start of a key the service echoed.

abcd's home folder and every folder in it are created private to your account (0700) whichever command creates them first, the hook included, and the files abcd keeps an index in are written 0600; an existing home keeps its mode.

A repository's model route in `.abcd/config.json` that cannot apply no longer takes the configuration down or overrides yours: a route naming a model a configured keyless provider does not list, or a provider this machine has not configured where the machine routes the same name, is skipped with a note and the machine's route applies.

The OpenAI-compatible adapter asks for a streamed answer, so a long delegated step on a reasoning model no longer fails at a 120-second deadline: a five-minute wait for the first byte, a two-minute idle limit and a 30-minute total cap replace it, a plain answer is still accepted, and any limit or cancel closes the connection so the service sees the client go.

The shell guard warns on a recursive delete of a chain of parents (`rm -rf ../..`, `../../.`, `../../*` and their quoted, trailing-slash and `$PWD`-led spellings), of the trailing-slash glob of the parent or of `$PWD` (`rm -rf ../*/`, `$PWD/*/`, `${PWD}/*/`), and of `../.`, as it already did on `..` and `../*`; no spelling that warned or blocked before is allowed now.

An after-merge fidelity audit that judges any criterion not met or inconclusive no longer reads as a pass: the intent stays shipped, its Audit Notes carry an audit-owed flag naming each such criterion and the receipt, and one issue carries the re-run, which a drain can take. A later passing verdict clears the flag with a dated line and resolves every open owed-check issue for that intent and receipt, flagged or not, and concurrent ingests of one verdict file one issue, not one each.

The build loop opens a lane for a ready step only while a helper is free to take it, so a waiting step has no worktree on disk; and a lane whose landing finds no preflight receipt waits for its full check on its own while the other lanes carry on, shown as `waiting for its full check (since HH:MM)`.

Pull requests the implement loop opens pass the attribution check: the body ends with `Assisted-by: abcd:<version>` and one `Assisted-by:` line per model the lane's receipts reported, and the step refuses before calling the forge when a receipt reports no model.
The site's authorship tally counts commits declaring `Assisted-by: abcd:<version>` as their own figure, composed by abcd, beneath the trailer chart, never as a model, a vendor or assistance.

Setup and embark agree on a conventions file they cannot write: an AGENTS.md that is a folder, a FIFO or unreadable raises `marker.unreadable`, and a project folder that cannot take a new file raises `marker.unwritable`, each required and not offered as a fix setup cannot make; `abcd embark probe` predicts the refusal or skip `embark from` then reports, and their notes name the file alone, not its full path.

When `abcd ahoy install`'s settings change does not land or is declined, the result still reports the tools an earlier step installed and verified, and names each value flag it did not apply, such as `--visibility` or `--docs-target`, with its value, why, and how to apply it.

abcd's own setup questions keep the limits its question check enforces: each fits 24 rows at 80 columns with at most four options and every fact kept, the conventions-file question by dropping the two choices setup no longer writes.

The bare status board fits the terminal's width (80 columns off a terminal) with a hanging indent, prints its first three rows as words rather than raw values, indents its levels at two, four and six columns, and lists the next-up intent under Now alone.

A ledger verb that refuses now writes nothing: resolve, wontfix, link, defer, remedy, promote, disposition and admit over an id the ledger does not hold, and a malformed disposition of an item it does hold, exit 2 and leave no `.iss-alloc.lock` behind.

`abcd docs fidelity record` and `docs fidelity --apply` read a verdict's brief chapter the same way: the file name, the name under `04-surfaces/` and the repository path are accepted and saved as the file name, and any other path is refused when it is recorded rather than at apply.

The release cut's dry run marks each targeted intent the cut will move to the next release (`; the cut moves it to next`) and leaves a target beyond the cut unmarked, and the ingest moves exactly those.

The note under each derived changelog section now says a breaking change is an Added line that states the break, so a breaking release no longer opens with a sentence its own breaking lines contradict; sections already cut keep their text.
When `abcd site build` adds missing interface labels to `ui.json` and then fails, it names each label it wrote before the error, so a changed file never goes unmentioned.

`abcd lint`'s privacy rule no longer reports a LAN hostname for a lower-case Go selector chain passed as a call argument in a tracked `.go` file; every other file, and every redactor, keeps the full check.

Site pages no longer scroll sideways on a narrow phone: the record dashboard at 360 and 390 px, and record pages whose title or source path holds a long unbroken run, such as a timestamp-id ADR's path, now wrap. The overflow audit samples those records and names the element that widens the page, skipping any inside its own scrolling panel.

The command pages for `ahoy`, `capture`, `docs`, `history`, `implement`, `ingest` and `launch` now match the binary in the ten lines the v0.12.0 docs review found. Three v0.12.0 notes are corrected here: the ban on the word maintainer is a pattern in abcd's own repository's docs-lint settings, not a rule bundled with docs-lint; the v0.12.0 opening note's claim that changes to earlier behaviour go unclaimed sat above two breaking lines filed under Added; and only the prompt-submit salvage hook declares the 120-second timeout, while the other two keep the host's default.

**Breaking: the build loop names a lane's stages `stage`, not `step`.** A spec's pieces keep the word step; what a lane goes through (`worktree`, `brief`, `implement`, `validate`, `land`) is a stage in every JSON field that carries one: `performed` becomes `performed_stage` and `step` becomes `stage` in `abcd implement step --json` and `abcd implement receipt --json`, a loop refusal's `refusal.step` becomes `refusal.stage`, a lane's `lane.step` under `status.now` in `abcd --json` becomes `lane.stage`, and `abcd implement check --json` and the refusal it logs carry `stage`, with an operand outside its five refused as an `unknown stage`. The run state file moves to schema version 8: a run begun on v0.11.1 (schema version 1) is read as it stands and rewritten at version 8 by its next `implement step` or `receipt`, which an older abcd cannot read, so finish a run with the abcd that will keep driving it. A script, hook or host reading any of the old fields stops finding them; update it from the table in docs/how-to/upgrade-to-v0.12.0.md.

**Breaking: the command spellings kept for one release are gone.** `abcd ahoy dry-run`, `abcd ahoy identity-check`, `abcd version` (with `abcd version --check`), `abcd docs lint` and `abcd site check` are unknown commands, refused with exit 2; use `abcd ahoy --dry-run`, `abcd ahoy --identity`, `abcd --version`, `abcd update --check`, `abcd lint docs` and `abcd lint site`. Bare `abcd identity` and bare `abcd ahoy remote` now list their sub-verbs and exit 0 instead of naming a replacement; for the reports they gave, use `abcd lint identity` and `abcd ahoy --remote`. Search scripts, hooks and CI workflows for the old spellings; docs/how-to/upgrade-to-v0.12.0.md lists every replacement.

**A role can run through a command-line harness.** The machine's configuration enables a shipped runner with `runner.<name>` (the claude CLI, always launched with its bare flag so a target repository's hooks and servers do not run, or opencode) and routes a role to it with `roles.<role>.runner`; a role left unset runs on the host as before, and a repository that declares `runner.*` is refused. The runner gets the same brief, inputs and output contract as the host sub-agent, its answer is validated the same way and its transcript lands in abcd's own store. A runner's model route off its provider's allowlist is refused before anything launches, a harness binary or PATH directory another account can write is refused, and a model the claude harness reports outside a bounded plain shape counts as an unparsable answer, so it never reaches the run state. An absent, refusing or failing runner hands the role back to the host, each fallback writes a receipt naming the role, the runner, the reason and the route that ran, and the run summary counts fallbacks per runner and per role. So far the runners are proven against stand-in harnesses only: no real claude or opencode binary has yet run a role, and the fallback for a run with no host session is built in the core but not yet reachable from a surface.

**An OpenAI-compatible API adapter.** `oracle.api.<provider>` takes a `base_url`, a `key` given by name and a `models` allowlist, and a role or judgement pointed at `<provider>/<model>` runs over that protocol with the same prompt, inputs and output contract as the host sub-agent, its transcript captured into the same store and the provider, the model asked for and the model reported recorded per call; `abcd ahoy connect` sets a provider up. A model not on its provider's list is refused when the configuration is read, before any call. The allowlist alone decides: abcd bundles no vendor denylist, and an `oracle.denylist` entry the configuration writes still refuses a listed model it matches. With no provider configured nothing changes and no network call is made.

**One credential store for every external key.** `abcd ahoy credential <name>` explains what a credential unlocks and what works without it, and stores it in the home named with `--home`: `external` (an environment variable, or a field of another tool's configuration file, of which abcd keeps only the pointer), `abcd` (the owner-only `~/.abcd/credentials.json`) or `keychain` (the platform keychain, which the explanation recommends); the value is read from standard input, and nothing is asked interactively. The API adapter and the site setup resolve keys by name through the store, and a name that resolves to nothing is refused naming the command that stores it. The `abcd` home refuses to write inside a git working tree, including through a home directory that is itself a symlink into a checkout, and the store reads and writes its index through the one `~/.abcd` it opened. The keychain home is so far exercised in tests against a stand-in, not a live keychain.

**The status board shows Now, Next and Later.** Bare `abcd` and the site's Status page compute the block from the record and store nothing: Now lists every intent whose lane the build's state file shows started, with its lane state, and names the head of `abcd build next`'s pick order as next up; Next lists the planned intents the readiness gate reports READY, in pick order; Later gives the planned intents that are not READY, with the failing check, then drafts. An intent in a lane is listed under Now only. The text board gives Later as a count, while `abcd --json` and the site keep its rows. The next-up head passes the record checks `abcd build next` runs (open questions, the claim sections, `blocked_by`, the spec's steps), though not its peers check. A managed repository's `site-src/ui.json` written before the block's labels existed keeps building: `abcd site setup` and `abcd site build` add each missing label with abcd's default words and name it on stderr.

**An intent can name the release it must land by.** `abcd intent plan --target <vX.Y.Z|next>` or `abcd intent target <itd-N> <vX.Y.Z|next>` writes `target_release` on a planned intent, and record lint refuses it on a shipped or superseded one. `abcd launch --dry-run` and the release cut list every targeted intent not yet shipped, in text, in the receipt and in `--json`, and proceed; at the cut, each target the release passes becomes `next`, and the status board marks a targeted intent with its target.

**A cut release gets a retrospective.** `abcd reflect <release-tag>` (`/abcd:reflect`) runs an interview seeded by the intents the tag shipped, read the way the release cut reads them, with their audit notes and the release's changelog section, and writes `.abcd/development/retrospectives/<release-tag>/README.md`. A shipped intent with no audit notes is named and `abcd intent audit <itd-N>` offered first; a tag that shipped no intent is refused. A packed lifeboat carries every retrospective, and embarking from one shows the predecessor lessons most like the new voyage's brief. A retrospective written while an embark runs makes the embark fail loudly rather than being replaced.

**A coherence pre-pass before the planning interview.** `abcd intent prepass <itd-N>` assembles the brief's invariants, the principles and a one-line index of every other intent beside a draft for the host to judge, and `--findings-json` writes the resulting questions into the planning brief under the local tier: each invariant the draft appears to conflict with, quoting both lines; each sibling it overlaps, with the four answers (keep both, bundle, supersede, refine) and any recommendation given in prose, never as a marked option; and each concern it cannot anchor to a named record, marked unanchored. The draft and its siblings are left unchanged.

**The brief must describe what ships.** In a repository that carries a brief, `abcd spec close` refuses to move an intent to shipped, and the release cut refuses over every intent shipped since the last tag, while the brief lags a surface: a deterministic layer refuses, with no oracle, any verb, sub-verb or agent no brief chapter names, and a host-delegated layer refuses on a confirmed false sentence and fails closed when no reviewer answers. `abcd docs fidelity` runs the gate, `--report` only reports, `--apply` writes the reviewer's drafted brief edits and flags each for review, `--autonomous` does the same for an unattended run, and `abcd docs fidelity record --verdict-json` records a verdict. No backlog file exempts a surface, a recorded verdict that names a false brief sentence cannot let the change through, and a drafted sentence or replacement spanning lines or over 2048 bytes is refused.

**A dependency bump can land without a person re-authoring it.** `abcd launch scaffold --dependency-reauthor` writes a workflow that re-authors a declared bot's bump as the repository owner when its diff touches only one declared ecosystem's manifest and lock file, names the bot and the workflow in the message with `Assisted-by: None`, updates the pull request and records each re-authoring; any other diff, bot or ecosystem is left alone and the run says which test it failed. The attribution gate is unchanged and still refuses the bot's original commit. The workflow is proven offline so far: the first live bump waits on the repository's GitHub App and its secrets.

**Session URLs and tool footers are kept out of committed text and the build loop's posts.** A live agent-session URL and a tool's generated-with footer are refused by `abcd lint`'s privacy rule in any committed file, by record-lint's `harness_leak` rule in the record and the docs, and by `abcd lint outbound`, which judges a commit message or any text given to it. The build loop strips either shape from the pull-request title and body it posts. Nothing scrubs other posts, such as a hand-opened pull request, an issue or a comment, so re-read and strip those after creating them.

**abcd names the product thinker or the technical facilitator, never the maintainer.** The command pages, rules, brief, principles, docs and rendered text say which of the two roles they mean, and docs-lint's banned-token list refuses the word maintainer.

**The rules loader teaches the shell hazards before shell work.** A SHELL domain is built on every rules load from the hazard registry the guard enforces, one lesson per entry and one recall term per command head; a repository's own `.abcd/guard.json` entries are taught marked `(repo)`, and a `guard.json` the guard refuses is named on stderr and never taught. A repository entry's `why` and `successor` are capped at 1,024 bytes, so one entry cannot crowd the other domains out of the injection budget; under a disabled registry each lesson opens `Hazard (guard off)` rather than claiming a refusal; and an override that withholds lessons names the repository's own among them.

**An armed gitleaks reaches every scan.** Capture, history, memory, the launch scan, the privacy lint, `disembark pack` and the other write paths report what an opted-in gitleaks finds, not the history capture alone. With gitleaks armed but not installed, the launch scan and `pack` fail closed, the privacy lint errors, and the write paths write on the native scanner and name the gap in their receipt, `abcd implement record --transcript` included.

**The implement run log counts agents and says what it cannot see.** `abcd implement log` counts the agents a session's own `agent_start` and `agent_end` lines declare alive, refuses an `agent_start` past the session's ceiling, and takes a `ceiling_overrun` event; `abcd implement check` reports `agents_alive`, and `abcd implement report` counts overruns and their minutes per mode and session. `implement log` refuses a `lane_close`, `agent_start` or `agent_end` missing a field the report needs, and the report names lines lacking a required field (`missing_fields`) and events whose lines stop more than six hours before the run's last line (`coverage`). An agent started outside the log stays invisible to the count.

`abcd hook prompt-router --json` writes `{text, injected, active}`, naming the full active-domain set on every prompt, so a client that snapshots injected rules can drop a domain that left the set; the kill switch is an empty list, and a domain that leaves and returns is injected again.

A stored transcript records its route in `source_kind` (`native` or `import`) and the tool that produced it in a new `source_tool`, so an imported transcript keeps its source harness; records written before the split read under both labels without a rewrite.

`abcd build --session <id>` claims the intent in the shared run state when it creates the run, so another checkout building the same intent is refused at its peers check from the start; a build without `--session` holds no claim and says so.
`abcd launch manifests --tree public|dev [--root <dir>]` runs the manifest lockstep check over a named tree, read-only, exiting 0 when consistent, 1 on drift and 2 when unreadable.

The filing-time match against the record runs on every route that files an issue: `abcd inbox promote`, the intent consistency pass, the reading ingest and the promote of a reading item, as well as `abcd capture`.

`abcd ahoy remote apply` and `abcd site setup` explain a missing gh and offer its Homebrew install, run only on a yes typed at a terminal; `--yes`, a piped answer and a run with no terminal decline with the command to run, and `abcd ahoy --remote` never installs.
`abcd capture wontfix --duplicates <iss-N|itd-N,...>` writes the typed `duplicates` link, checked for shape, self-reference and existence before anything is written.

record-lint's `stale_edge` rule flags a planned or draft intent whose `builds_on` or `blocked_by` names a superseded intent, naming the successor its chain ends at, and `edge_cycle` flags a `builds_on`/`blocked_by` cycle naming every record on it; both warn.

A committed `.githooks/prepare-commit-msg` writes the `Assisted-by:` trailer from `git config abcd.assistedBy` when git prepares a message, so a plain `git revert`, a cherry-pick, an amend or a squash reaches the attribution gate with its trailer; with the key unset it writes nothing, and it never writes `None`.

The prefer-sota principle, and the bundled OPINIONS rule that points at it, say a remedy proposed for an issue or chosen in an autonomous run cites its grounds, including a primary-source state-of-the-art check where the fix depends on outside practice.
The ready-intent and open-spec next moves say that closing the spec ships the intent when no other open spec names it.

**`abcd guard` blocks a recursive delete of the root or the home.** The bundled registry's `rm-rf-root-or-home` blocks `rm -rf` of `/`, `/*`, `~`, `$HOME` and `${HOME}` and their slash and star forms, and `rm-rf-working-directory` warns on `*`, `.`, `..`, `./*`, `../*` and `.*`, where a bare `rm -rf /` was allowed. The compare reads the spellings a shell resolves to the same place, bare and through `sh -c` or `bash -c`: repeated separators and `/./` segments, a `..` folded after the root, the home, `$PWD` or a relative start, a run of `*` as one star, a dot-led glob segment that can match `..` (bracket expressions included), trailing-slash globs such as `/*/` and `~/*/`, and a separator run before `$HOME`.

The root-or-home rule reads a variable operand as the set of texts it can print: its written spelling (`$HOME`, `"$HOME"`, `${HOME}`, a backslash-newline inside the name, a brace group), a default's or alternative's word however it is quoted (ANSI-C and locale strings included), a trim, replacement or substring that can leave only `/` or the home, indirect, positional and special parameters such as `$!`, and an expansion that can print nothing beside a root, so `rm -rf ${DIR:-$HOME}`, `rm -rf ${X%%*}/` and `rm -rf $!/` block while `${DIR%/}`, `${f%.txt}` and `${p##*/}` stay allowed.

A line that assigns `IFS`, directly or through a name built from an expansion in any place bash assigns through (`export`, `declare`, `read`, `printf -v`, `eval`, arithmetic and the rest), makes the root-or-home rule treat unquoted defaults, alternatives, trims, replacements and `$HOME` or `$PWD` as split, so `IFS=x; rm -rf ${U:-x/x}` blocks.

The root-or-home rule no longer blocks everyday clean lines: a positional slice such as `rm -rf "${@:2}"` reads as the parameters' value, and a colon default such as `rm -rf "${1:-build}"/*` is read without an empty value it cannot print, while `${@:-w}` and `${*:-w}` keep the empty value their parameter-count test allows.

A command name, subcommand or flag spelled with a bracket expression the guard cannot decide, such as `r[[:lower:]] -rf /` or `git clea[[:lower:]] -fd`, is compared with that span read as a star, so it blocks or warns as its expansion would.

The shell guard reads more of what bash runs: a parameter expansion is an unknown word, so a dash glued to a variable (`git push --$X`) or a variable in command position blocks as its command-substitution twin does; kill-by-search follows a search fed into `xargs kill` through an unquoted here-document or an inherited pipe; a here-document a substitution opens and never reads refuses the line; and a pending here-document beside an unterminated substitution no longer panics the tokenizer.
The bundled guard registry blocks `abcd source ledger --flip`, leaving the flip to a public citation to the person.

The guard's command page and hook help state that it adjudicates only the shell and question tool calls the hook manifest hands it, so a hazardous call through any other tool is neither checked nor warned about.

**A refusal no longer repeats a value a host payload chose.** The ideate recorder, lifeboat review, intent audit, the reading ingest, the intent consistency ingest, scribe, release, the implement loop's lane receipt and the memory page ingest describe a refused value by its length or redact it through the canonical scanner instead of quoting it; the memory writer seals the secret in a page filename it refuses; and the owed-audit listing withholds a dead-letter reason's tokens that name the local tier.

The secret scanner finds a token glued behind a letter, a digit or an underscore, in the percent-decoded and JSON-unescaped views too, so the launch scan, every store-before-commit redactor and refusal redaction seal it; a sweep that cannot be built fails those paths closed.

`abcd launch ship --changelog-json` scans the rendered changelog section and release page with the canonical scanner and refuses a secret, a key, or the caller's own home or identity with reason `privacy`, naming the kind and the line but never the matched text.

The payload byte scan reads more document metadata for a person's name: EXIF and TIFF person tags (Artist, Copyright, XPAuthor, CameraOwnerName) and a Canon MakerNote's owner name, IPTC person datasets and their text-keyed siblings, and PDF text strings written in hex or with octal escapes, so a short single-token name there is kept as a finding rather than dropped as chance.
The scanner no longer masks the repository owner's handle in an `owner/repo` slug that names a sibling repository on GitHub; the owner alone and other owners stay findings.

The privacy lint reads an escaped Windows home path at any escaping depth, record-lint's `harness_leak` rule reads the issue ledger, and Homebrew's Linux prefix reads as a system account rather than a person's home.
The public banlist gates the plugin surfaces the shipped artefact carries (`commands/`, `agents/` and `hooks/`), as it gates the README and `docs/`.
A custom secret pattern whose boundary-free form cannot compile no longer turns the scanner's junction search into a per-byte walk for the whole pattern set.

**Output no longer prints a checkout's absolute path.** The status board and `abcd --json`'s `dir`, `abcd peers`, the capture verbs and the other surfaces show a path under the home directory home-relative and one outside it by its directory name, and the board's first line masks escape sequences and bidi controls in the checkout's name.

**Every file abcd trusts in `~/.abcd` is reached through the directory it judged.** A symlinked `~/.abcd` is refused by the machine credential store, the PATH-entry and cache-attestation records, the hook shims and the history registry, as the rules loader already refused it; each level below the home is opened by descriptor, and one every account can write or another account owns is refused; the status-line settings are read through the same check; the history registry loads and writes under the lock it took; and lock files are created owner-only.

Two abcd processes on one machine no longer make one refuse its own `~/.abcd` configuration as swapped: a file atomically renamed into place between the check and the read is judged afresh, up to eight times.

The append primitive refuses a symlink planted between its check and its open, the implement run state refuses a symlinked log and reads a claim whose session or lane is not a name as unreadable, and every lock descriptor is close-on-exec, so a child that outlives its parent no longer keeps a lock held.

ahoy's rewrites of `.abcd/config.json`, the `.gitignore` block and the agent-instructions marker block, and the release cut's CHANGELOG writes, run under a file lock; the store locks move onto shared primitives that still exclude an older binary, and the history store's lock gives up after two minutes instead of waiting without end.
The update notice is shown once across any number of concurrent session starts.

Transcript records are written owner-only (0600) under an owner-only chain, a records directory or legacy record left wider is narrowed, and a records directory another account owns is refused naming that account, without write wording on a read verb.

A symlinked `.abcd`, `.abcd/development` or `specs/` is refused rather than followed by the spec store, the ADR mint lock and scribe's run directory; the bare reading render lists its stages through the one root it opened; and the drain rule refuses a linked decision store.
`abcd update` creates its staging file exclusively and without following links, so a symlink planted at `.abcd.new` is removed, never written through.

`abcd ahoy install` on a cold cache writes no PATH entry a plugin update would strand and names the install one-liner to run first; it removes abcd-owned dangling PATH entries once its target works, never an unowned one; and a stale binary refuses before any write, the `--bin-dir` writability probe included.

After an update abcd says `abcd updated from X to Y` once, from the installer, `abcd update` or, for a swap the hook made unseen, the next session start; `abcd --version` and bare `ahoy` note when the session's plugin root differs from the running binary's.

ahoy's config gaps name the flag that answers them (`--visibility`, `--docs-target`, `--oracle-backend`, `--scan-deep`), a `--yes` run says up front that values are still asked, every JSON list renders empty as `[]` rather than `null`, an existing `.abcd/rules.json` is kept rather than replaced by the skeleton, and the drain-rule offer is asked only at a terminal, so a piped answer stream no longer shifts.
Consent questions no longer read standard input redirected from `/dev/null` as a terminal, and a gitleaks or trufflehog that PATH resolves inside the checkout no longer counts as installed.

The hook shims refuse a PATH candidate whose file is world-writable, and every salvage hook entry that runs the bootstrap declares a status message; the every-prompt entry (UserPromptSubmit) also declares a 120-second timeout, while the before-command (PreToolUse) and before-compaction (PreCompact) entries declare none and take the host's default.

A repository route in `.abcd/config.json` with a malformed name or value is skipped with one sanitised diagnostic instead of taking every provider command down; `ahoy connect`, `ahoy credential` and bare `ahoy` name each skipped route; a route whose agent's role setting does not point at the routed connection is refused naming `oracle.roles.<agent>`; and an API answer that reports no model is refused, so every recorded call names what answered.

`abcd drain` hands a deferred record back when the checkout holds no release tag or only one older than its `deferred_after`, naming `git fetch --tags`, and refuses a candidate record with a duplicated key or an id its filename contradicts.

The build loop's records commit names the model the lane's receipts report in its `Assisted-by:` trailer and runs the repository's hooks; a zero-padded issue key is refused; quoted text in a lane brief can no longer close its fence; and a handed-back run names its run directory as the way out.

The blocked pre-start check settles a blocker whose supersession chain ends at an accepted ADR or in `disciplines/`; every backoff in the run log carries its reason and measured minutes; and `abcd implement report` counts a session that joined up to a minute before a window's mode was set in that window.
Under `--json`, an unknown flag is answered with the error envelope on stdout at exit 2, and `abcd update --json` writes one document on a refusal.

`abcd help --agent` refuses naming `abcd --help --agent`, the people block reads the same under `--help` and `--help --agent`, and the CLI reference says the second form adds the agents-and-hosts verbs.

The `spec_lifecycle` rule refuses a planned intent whose only spec is closed and a shipped intent with a spec still open.

A provenance restamp beside an out-of-vocabulary origin is refused.

The filing-time match reports an unreadable `open/` or `resolved/` folder as unread instead of comparing against nothing.
The stray-ledger note no longer names the checkout's own ledger as a stray when the working directory is spelled in a different case on a case-insensitive filesystem.

The memory page-filename bar refuses secret patterns only, the bare memory board prints its staleness warning with the verb that fixes it, and the lint report renders untrusted text cleaned.

The tool installer no longer offers trufflehog, which abcd never runs; an install step's wait is bounded even when a descendant holds its output; the Homebrew explanation states the network fetch and install analytics; and one CI detector refuses an install on any runner.
A checkout entered through a symlinked path is no longer refused by `ahoy install`'s local-tier check or by `implement receipt`.

The lifeboat verbs, `history reconstruct --out` and `reading assemble --out` prove every directory level of their output path, so a committed symlink above it cannot redirect a write.

Staging a transcript locks per session or agent, so a burst of simultaneous sub-agent completions no longer loses transcripts.

A repository or user override of a guardrail domain (COMMITTING, LOAD, PII) names on stderr every bundled recall keyword and rule its list leaves out, so a later bundled upgrade is no longer withheld silently.

In a source checkout a plugin-root binary that trails the source tip is warned about at session start, and a dev-stamped setup version no longer reports a permanent version transition against every release.
`abcd update`'s refusal for a PATH entry it will not replace says where the entry leads and what it examined, and no longer calls a regular file behind a symlink something it is not.

The badge and `abcd mode` name the technical facilitator in the same words.
The persona checks see a `says <Name>,` attribution as well as `said <Name>,`.
